title: How to Set Up Google Client ID and Secret for Gmail
content:
## Why you need Google OAuth credentials

To connect Gmail accounts in Pigeon using **Google sign-in (OAuth)** instead of app passwords, you need to create your own **Google Cloud OAuth client** and add the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** in Pigeon. This lets you authorize Gmail in the browser without storing your Gmail password. Your plan must allow Gmail (e.g. Premium); if the app does not have a default OAuth client, you must add your own credentials in **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**.

## Step 1: Get Client ID and Secret from Google Cloud Console

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Create a project or select an existing one (top bar).
3. Open **APIs & Services** → **Credentials** (left menu, or use the search).
4. Click **+ Create Credentials** → **OAuth client ID**.
5. If prompted, configure the **OAuth consent screen** first: choose **External** (or Internal for Google Workspace), add app name (e.g. Pigeon), support email, and save.
6. Back in **Create OAuth client ID**:
   - **Application type**: choose **Web application**.
   - **Name**: e.g. "Pigeon Gmail".
   - Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, click **Add URI**. Do not type the URL manually—**get it from the dashboard**: in Pigeon go to **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**, open the form to add Google credentials, and **copy the Authorized redirect URI** shown there. Paste that URI into Google Cloud.
   - Save. Google will show the **Client ID** (looks like `xxxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com`) and **Client Secret** (looks like `GOCSPX-xxxxx`). Copy both; the secret is shown only once (you can regenerate it later if needed).

## Step 2: Add the redirect URI (critical)

In your OAuth client, under **Authorized redirect URIs**, you must add the URI **exactly as shown in the dashboard**. In Pigeon go to **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**, open the form where you enter your Google Client ID and Secret—the page shows the **Authorized redirect URI** you need. Copy it from there and paste it into Google Cloud; do not type it from documentation or guess. Google will reject sign-in if the redirect URI does not match exactly.

## Step 3: Save credentials in Pigeon

1. In Pigeon, go to **Settings** → **Integrations** (or **Settings** and open the Integrations tab).
2. Find the **Gmail** section.
3. If you see **Add your Google OAuth credentials** or **Google Client ID / Google Client Secret**, click to expand or open the form.
4. Enter:
   - **Google Client ID**: paste the Client ID (e.g. `xxxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com`).
   - **Google Client Secret**: paste the Client Secret (e.g. `GOCSPX-xxxxx`).
5. Click **Save**. The app stores the secret securely and never returns it in the UI.
6. After saving, you can **Connect Gmail** with Google (OAuth): click **Connect with Google** and complete the browser flow; your Gmail account will be added as an inbox.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials.
- [ ] Create OAuth client ID (Web application).
- [ ] Add Authorized redirect URI: copy from dashboard (Settings → Integrations → Gmail, when adding credentials)
- [ ] Copy Client ID and Client Secret.
- [ ] Settings → Integrations → Gmail: paste Client ID and Secret, Save.
- [ ] Connect Gmail with Google (OAuth) from the same Integrations section.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Google OAuth credentials not set"** — Add your Client ID and Secret in Settings → Integrations → Gmail and save.
- **Redirect URI mismatch** — Ensure the redirect URI in Google Cloud matches exactly the one shown in the dashboard (copy from Settings → Integrations → Gmail when adding credentials).
- **App not verified** — For External consent, unverified apps show a warning; you can still choose "Advanced" → "Go to Pigeon (unsafe)" to continue during testing. For production, consider submitting the app for verification.
- **Secret not shown again** — If you lose the secret, create a new one in Google Cloud (Credentials → your OAuth client → reset secret) and update it in Pigeon.
excerpt: Step-by-step: get Google Client ID and Secret from Cloud Console, add the Gmail callback redirect URI, and save them in Pigeon Settings → Integrations to connect Gmail with OAuth.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Connect Gmail with an App Password (Without OAuth)
content:
## Why use an App Password?

If you prefer not to use Google OAuth (sign-in with Google), you can connect Gmail to Pigeon using an **App Password**. This is a 16-character password generated by Google that lets Pigeon send and receive email on your behalf without using your main Gmail password. Your plan must allow Gmail; you can add accounts from **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**.

## Before you start

1. Your Gmail account must have **2-Step Verification** turned on. Google only issues App Passwords for accounts with 2-Step Verification.
2. You will need to generate the App Password from your Google Account settings (not from Pigeon).

## Step 1: Turn on 2-Step Verification (if needed)

1. Go to [Google Account](https://myaccount.google.com/) and sign in.
2. In the left menu, click **Security**.
3. Under "How you sign in to Google," find **2-Step Verification** and click it.
4. Follow the steps to turn on 2-Step Verification (phone or authenticator app).

## Step 2: Create an App Password

1. In your Google Account, go to **Security** → **2-Step Verification** (you must be on 2-Step Verification first).
2. Scroll to **App passwords** and click it.
3. You may need to sign in again. In "Select app" choose **Mail**, and in "Select device" choose **Other** and type a name like "Pigeon".
4. Click **Generate**. Google will show a 16-character password (with spaces; you can ignore the spaces). Copy this password—you will paste it into Pigeon. You won't see it again.

## Step 3: Add Gmail in Pigeon with App Password

1. In Pigeon, go to **Settings** (sidebar) and open the **Integrations** tab.
2. Find the **Gmail** section. If you have the option to use "With App Password" or "Connect via App Password," click it.
3. Click **Connect via App Password** (or **Add Gmail account** and choose App Password).
4. In the dialog:
   - **Gmail Address**: Enter the full Gmail address (e.g. you@gmail.com).
   - **App Password**: Paste the 16-character App Password you copied from Google (with or without spaces—both work).
5. Click **Connect** or **Save**. Pigeon will verify the credentials and add the account as an inbox.
6. The new Gmail account will appear under **Inbox Accounts** (sidebar → **Inbox Accounts**) and in **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**.

## After connecting

- You can use this Gmail account when creating or editing campaigns: choose **Gmail** as the sender type and select this inbox.
- You can connect multiple Gmail accounts (within your plan limit) by repeating the steps with different addresses and App Passwords.
- To disconnect later, go to **Settings → Integrations → Gmail**, find the account, and use the disconnect or remove option.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Google Account → Security → 2-Step Verification turned on.
- [ ] Security → App passwords → Generate for Mail / Other (Pigeon).
- [ ] Copy the 16-character App Password.
- [ ] Pigeon → Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect via App Password.
- [ ] Enter Gmail address and App Password, then Connect.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Invalid credentials"** — Make sure 2-Step Verification is on and you used the App Password (not your normal Gmail password). Generate a new App Password if needed.
- **App passwords option missing** — You must enable 2-Step Verification first; the "App passwords" option appears only after that.
- **Account already connected** — If the same Gmail appears twice or you get a conflict, disconnect the existing one in Settings → Integrations → Gmail and add again with the correct App Password.
excerpt: Connect Gmail to Pigeon using a Google App Password: enable 2-Step Verification, create an App Password, then add the address and password in Settings → Integrations → Gmail.

title: How to Add and Verify Your Sending Domain in Pigeon
content:
## Why verify a domain?

To send email from your own domain (e.g. you@yourcompany.com) instead of Gmail, you need to **add and verify** the domain in Pigeon. Verification is done by adding DNS records at your domain provider. Once verified, you can add SMTP inbox accounts for that domain and use them in campaigns. Go to **Domains** in the sidebar to get started.

## Step 1: Add your domain

1. In Pigeon, click **Domains** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **Add Domain** (or the button to add a new domain).
3. Enter your domain name (e.g. **yourcompany.com**). Do not include http:// or www—just the domain.
4. Save or continue. Pigeon will create the domain and show you the DNS records you need to add.

## Step 2: Add DNS records

Pigeon will show you the exact records to add. Typically you need:

- **SPF** — A TXT record that authorizes Pigeon (or your email provider) to send mail for your domain.
- **DKIM** — One or more TXT records that prove your emails are legitimately from your domain.
- **MX** (if you use Pigeon for receiving) — So replies can be delivered to your inbox.

1. In the Domains page, select your domain to see **DNS records** or **Verification**.
2. Copy each record: **Type**, **Name/Host**, **Value**, and **TTL** if shown.
3. Log in to your domain registrar or DNS provider (e.g. GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Namecheap, your hosting panel).
4. Add each record in the DNS management area. The Name might be shown as @ or your domain; use exactly what Pigeon shows.
5. Save changes at your DNS provider. Propagation can take from a few minutes up to 48 hours.

## Step 3: Verify the domain

1. Back in Pigeon, open **Domains** and select your domain.
2. Click **Verify** or **Verify domain**. Pigeon will check that the DNS records are present and correct.
3. If verification succeeds, the domain status will show as verified (e.g. a green check or "Verified").
4. If it fails, double-check that you added every required record and that the values match exactly (no extra spaces). Wait a bit for DNS propagation and try again.

## Step 4: Use the domain for sending

Once verified, you can:
- Add **Inbox Accounts** (SMTP) for addresses on this domain (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com).
- In **Campaigns**, choose **SMTP** as the sender type and select those inboxes.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Domains → Add Domain → enter domain name.
- [ ] Copy all required DNS records (SPF, DKIM, etc.) from Pigeon.
- [ ] Add the records at your DNS provider.
- [ ] Domains → Verify.
- [ ] Add SMTP inboxes for the domain in Inbox Accounts when ready.

## Troubleshooting

- **Verification fails** — Ensure each record type, name, and value matches exactly. Check for typos and wait for DNS propagation.
- **Record already exists** — If you have an existing SPF record, you may need to merge values (include Pigeon's include:... in your existing SPF string). The dashboard or support can guide you.
- **Domain not showing** — Refresh the Domains page; if you just added the domain, it should appear in the list.
excerpt: Add your sending domain in Domains, add the required DNS records (SPF, DKIM, etc.) at your provider, then verify in Pigeon so you can send from your own domain.

title: How to Set Up Reply-To (IMAP) for Campaign Replies
content:
## What is Reply-To (IMAP)?

When contacts reply to your campaign emails, you can have those replies delivered to a specific inbox that Pigeon monitors. **Reply-To** lets you choose which address (Gmail or an IMAP mailbox) receives the replies. You can also add **Reply-To IMAP** configs so Pigeon can read replies from an external mailbox (e.g. support@yourcompany.com) and surface them in the **Inbox** tab. Set this up in **Settings → Integrations**.

## Step 1: Open Integrations

1. In Pigeon, go to **Settings** (sidebar).
2. Open the **Integrations** tab.
3. Find the **Reply-To** or **Campaign replies** section.

## Step 2: Choose default reply-to for campaigns

1. Under Reply-To you will see options such as **Use sending inbox** (replies go to the same address that sent the email) or **Specific Gmail / IMAP**.
2. If you want replies to go to a specific Gmail: select **Gmail** and choose the Gmail account from the dropdown (these are the same accounts you connected under the Gmail section).
3. If you use a custom domain and have an IMAP mailbox for replies, you can add an **IMAP** config (see below) and then select it as the reply-to.
4. Save. When you create or edit a campaign, you can override the reply-to per campaign (e.g. use a different address for one campaign).

## Step 3: Add a Reply-To IMAP config (optional)

If replies go to an email address that is not a Gmail connected in Pigeon (e.g. support@yourdomain.com via your host's IMAP):

1. In **Settings → Integrations**, find **Reply-To IMAP** or **IMAP configs**.
2. Click **Add** or **Add IMAP account**.
3. Enter the mailbox details: **Email**, **IMAP host** (e.g. imap.yourprovider.com), **Port** (usually 993 for SSL), **Username** (often the full email), **Password** (or app password).
4. Save. Pigeon will test the connection. Once added, you can select this mailbox as the reply-to for campaigns so replies appear in Pigeon's Inbox.

## Step 4: Use reply-to in campaigns

When creating or editing a campaign (**Campaigns** → **New** or **Edit**), look for **Reply-To** or **Reply to address**. You can leave it as default (from Settings) or pick a specific Gmail or IMAP mailbox. Replies to that campaign will then be associated with the correct inbox in the **Inbox** view.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Settings → Integrations → Reply-To section.
- [ ] Set default: Gmail account or IMAP (if configured).
- [ ] Optional: Add Reply-To IMAP config for non-Gmail reply addresses.
- [ ] Per campaign: set reply-to if you want a different address for that campaign.

## Troubleshooting

- **Replies not showing** — Ensure the reply-to address is one Pigeon can read (Gmail connected or IMAP config added) and that the campaign is using that reply-to.
- **IMAP connection failed** — Check host, port, username, and password. Many providers require an app password instead of the normal password.
excerpt: Set the default reply-to (Gmail or IMAP) in Settings → Integrations so campaign replies are delivered to the right inbox and visible in the Inbox tab.

title: How to Add SMTP Inbox Accounts for Your Domain
content:
## Why use SMTP inboxes?

SMTP inboxes let you send campaign emails from your own domain (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com) instead of Gmail. You add them after you have **verified your domain** in **Domains**. Each SMTP inbox is tied to a verified domain and uses the credentials from your email provider (e.g. SendGrid, your host, or another SMTP service).

## Before you start

1. **Verify your domain** in **Domains** (add DNS records and click Verify).
2. Have your SMTP details ready: host, port, username, and password (or API key if your provider uses that). Your email provider’s docs or support can give you these.

## Step 1: Open Inbox Accounts

1. In Pigeon, click **Inbox Accounts** in the sidebar.
2. Click **Add Inbox** or **New inbox** (or go to **Inbox Accounts** → **New** if you have a dedicated page).

## Step 2: Choose SMTP and domain

1. When adding an inbox, select **SMTP** or **Domain inbox** (not Gmail).
2. Select the **domain** you verified. The list shows only domains that are verified.
3. Enter the **email address** for this inbox (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com). It must be on the selected domain.

## Step 3: Enter SMTP credentials

1. Enter the **SMTP host** (e.g. smtp.sendgrid.net or mail.yourprovider.com).
2. Enter the **port** (often 587 for TLS or 465 for SSL; your provider will specify).
3. Enter **username** and **password** (or API key). These are usually provided by your email/SMTP provider.
4. If there is a **Test connection** or **Verify** button, use it to confirm the credentials work.
5. Save. The new SMTP inbox will appear in **Inbox Accounts** and may show a status such as **Warming** or **Ready** (if warmup applies to your plan).

## Step 4: Use the SMTP inbox in campaigns

1. Go to **Campaigns** → create or edit a campaign.
2. Under sender, choose **SMTP** (or "Domain" / "Inbox").
3. Select the domain (if asked) and then the SMTP inbox(es) you want to use for sending.
4. Save the campaign. Emails will be sent from that SMTP address.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Domain verified in Domains.
- [ ] Inbox Accounts → Add Inbox → SMTP / Domain.
- [ ] Select domain and enter email address.
- [ ] Enter SMTP host, port, username, password; test if available.
- [ ] Use the new inbox in Campaigns when selecting sender.

## Troubleshooting

- **Domain not in list** — Verify the domain in Domains first and refresh the page.
- **Connection failed** — Double-check host, port, username, and password. Use TLS/SSL as your provider recommends.
- **Warm up required** — New SMTP inboxes may need to complete warmup before full sending; check the Warmup section and status in Inbox Accounts.
excerpt: After verifying your domain in Domains, add SMTP inbox accounts in Inbox Accounts with your provider's host, port, and credentials, then use them in campaigns.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Add Your First Gmail or SMTP Inbox
content:
## Why add an inbox?

Pigeon sends campaign emails from **inboxes**—either Gmail accounts or SMTP (domain) accounts. Before you can run a campaign, you need at least one inbox connected. Gmail is quick to set up; SMTP is used when you want to send from your own domain (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com).

## Option A: Add your first Gmail inbox

1. Go to **Settings** (sidebar) → **Integrations** tab.
2. Find the **Gmail** section.
3. Connect using either:
   - **Connect with Google** (OAuth) — You need Google Client ID and Secret set first (see our blog on that). Click **Connect with Google** and sign in in the browser.
   - **Connect via App Password** — Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google Account, create an App Password, then in Pigeon enter your Gmail address and the App Password and click Connect.
4. After connecting, the Gmail account appears under **Inbox Accounts** (sidebar). You can add more Gmail accounts the same way, within your plan limit.

## Option B: Add your first SMTP inbox

1. **Verify your domain** first: go to **Domains**, add your domain, add the DNS records (SPF, DKIM, etc.) at your DNS provider, and click **Verify**.
2. Go to **Inbox Accounts** (sidebar) → **Add Inbox** or **New**.
3. Choose **SMTP** or **Domain inbox**, select your verified domain, and enter the email address (e.g. hello@yourcompany.com).
4. Enter your SMTP credentials (host, port, username, password) from your email provider. Use **Test connection** if available.
5. Save. The inbox appears in **Inbox Accounts** and may show warmup status.

## After adding

- **Inbox Accounts** lists all Gmail and SMTP inboxes. You can see status (Ready, Warming, etc.) and manage them.
- When creating a **Campaign**, you will choose **Gmail** or **SMTP** as sender type and select one or more of these inboxes.
- For new SMTP inboxes, consider using **Warmup** (if available on your plan) before sending large volume.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Gmail: Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect (OAuth or App Password).
- [ ] SMTP: Domains → verify domain; Inbox Accounts → Add Inbox → SMTP → enter credentials.
- [ ] Confirm the new inbox appears under Inbox Accounts.
excerpt: Add your first sending inbox: connect Gmail from Settings → Integrations (OAuth or App Password), or add an SMTP inbox from Inbox Accounts after verifying your domain.

title: How to Manage Inbox Accounts and See Warmup Status
content:
## Where to manage inboxes

All your sending inboxes (Gmail and SMTP) are listed under **Inbox Accounts** in the sidebar. From there you can see each inbox’s email, type (Gmail vs SMTP), status, warmup progress, and daily send count. You can also open settings for an inbox, pause or resume warmup, and remove inboxes you no longer need.

## Viewing inbox list and status

1. Click **Inbox Accounts** in the left sidebar.
2. The table (or cards) show for each inbox:
   - **Email** — The sending address.
   - **Type** — Gmail or SMTP.
   - **Status** — e.g. Ready, Warming, Paused, Warm up required, or Warning.
   - **Warmup** — Progress percentage or "Warmed" if applicable.
   - **Sent today** — How many emails sent from that inbox today (useful for daily limits).
3. Use this view to decide which inboxes to use in a campaign and whether any need warmup before use.

## Changing inbox settings

1. In **Inbox Accounts**, find the inbox and click **Settings**, **Edit**, or the gear icon (if available).
2. Depending on the inbox type you may be able to change labels, pause/resume warmup, or update credentials. Gmail accounts are usually managed from **Settings → Integrations → Gmail** (disconnect or add).
3. Save any changes. Status and warmup will update on the list.

## Understanding warmup status

- **Ready** — Inbox can be used for sending; warmup is complete or not required.
- **Warming** — Warmup is in progress; you can often send at a limited rate.
- **Warm up required** — Inbox is new or was paused; warmup should be started from the **Warmup** page.
- **Warning** — Warmup progress is below a threshold; consider pausing campaigns or increasing warmup.

For more detail, use the **Warmup** item in the sidebar to see timelines and control warmup per inbox.

## Removing an inbox

1. In **Inbox Accounts**, find the inbox.
2. Use **Delete**, **Remove**, or **Disconnect** (for Gmail, this may be in Settings → Integrations → Gmail).
3. Confirm. The inbox will no longer appear and cannot be selected in new campaigns. Existing campaigns that used it may need to be updated.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Inbox Accounts → view all inboxes and their status.
- [ ] Use status and warmup % to choose inboxes for campaigns.
- [ ] Open settings per inbox to pause/resume warmup or edit as needed.
- [ ] Remove or disconnect inboxes you no longer use.
excerpt: Use Inbox Accounts to view all Gmail and SMTP inboxes, see status and warmup progress, change settings, and remove inboxes you no longer need.

title: Understanding Inbox Status: Ready, Warming, and Warm Up Required
content:
## Why inbox status matters

Each sending inbox in Pigeon has a **status** that tells you whether it is safe to use for campaigns and how much you can send. Sending too much from a new or cold inbox can hurt deliverability and get emails marked as spam. Use the status in **Inbox Accounts** and **Warmup** to decide when to use an inbox.

## Status meanings

**Ready**
- The inbox is fully warmed or does not require warmup. You can use it in campaigns and send up to your plan’s and daily limits. This is the ideal state for sending.

**Warming**
- Warmup is in progress. Pigeon (or your setup) is gradually increasing sending volume for this inbox. You can often use it for campaigns at a reduced rate; check the Warmup page for recommended limits. Sending more than the warmup curve may hurt reputation.

**Warm up required**
- The inbox is new, was just added, or warmup has not been started. You should start warmup from the **Warmup** page before using it for full campaigns. Sending at full volume from this state is risky for deliverability.

**Warning**
- Warmup progress is below a safe threshold (e.g. low percentage or paused for a while). Consider pausing campaigns that use this inbox or increasing warmup until the status improves.

**Paused**
- Warmup or sending for this inbox has been paused. Resume from the Warmup page or inbox settings when you want to use it again.

## Where you see status

- **Inbox Accounts** — Each inbox shows a status badge (Ready, Warming, Warm up required, Warning, Paused).
- **Warmup** — The Warmup page shows a timeline and per-inbox progress; you can start, pause, or resume warmup there.
- **Campaigns** — When you select sender inboxes, you may see warnings if an inbox is not ready or has warmup required.

## What to do

- **Ready** — Use the inbox normally in campaigns.
- **Warming** — Use it only within the suggested warmup limits, or wait until it shows Ready.
- **Warm up required** — Go to Warmup, start warmup for that inbox, and wait until it reaches Warming or Ready.
- **Warning** — Ease off sending from that inbox and/or increase warmup until the warning clears.

## Summary

- Ready = safe to send. Warming = send within warmup limits. Warm up required = start warmup first. Warning = improve warmup or reduce sending.
excerpt: Learn what Ready, Warming, Warm up required, Warning, and Paused mean for your inboxes and when it is safe to use each for campaigns.

title: What Is Email Warmup and How to Use It in Pigeon
content:
## What is email warmup?

**Email warmup** is the process of gradually increasing the volume of email sent from a new or unused inbox so that providers (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) learn to trust it. If you send a lot of mail suddenly from a new address, it can be flagged as spam. Warmup sends a controlled amount of mail (often to internal or partner addresses) and builds a positive sending pattern so your real campaigns land in the inbox.

## Why Pigeon has warmup

Pigeon’s **Warmup** feature (available on supported plans) helps you warm up Gmail and SMTP inboxes before you use them for campaigns. The **Warmup** page in the sidebar shows which inboxes are warming, their progress, and lets you start, pause, or resume warmup.

## How to use warmup in Pigeon

1. Go to **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. You will see your inboxes (Gmail and/or SMTP) and their warmup state: not started, warming, paused, or complete.
3. For an inbox that shows **Warm up required** or **Start warmup**: click **Start** or **Enable warmup** so Pigeon begins the warmup sequence for that inbox.
4. Warmup runs over time (days to weeks depending on the curve). You can see progress (e.g. a percentage or chart) on the Warmup page and in **Inbox Accounts** (warmup status per inbox).
5. When an inbox reaches a sufficient warmup level, its status in Inbox Accounts will change to **Ready** or **Warming** (safe to use within limits). You can then use it in campaigns.
6. To **pause** warmup: use the Pause control on the Warmup page or in the inbox’s settings. To **resume**, click Resume.

## Best practices

- Start warmup for new inboxes before sending campaigns from them.
- Do not send large campaign volume from an inbox that is still in "Warm up required" or early "Warming".
- Use the recommended send limits shown for warming inboxes if you send from them during warmup.
- Keep warmup running until the inbox shows Ready (or your plan’s equivalent) for best deliverability.

## Summary

Warmup builds sender reputation gradually. In Pigeon, use the Warmup page to start, monitor, and pause/resume warmup for each inbox so your campaigns have the best chance to land in the inbox.
excerpt: Email warmup builds sender reputation for new inboxes. Learn what it is and how to start, monitor, and control warmup in Pigeon.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Start, Pause, or Resume Warmup for Your Inboxes
content:
## Where to control warmup

You start, pause, and resume warmup from the **Warmup** page in the sidebar. That page lists your inboxes (Gmail and SMTP) and shows each one’s warmup state and progress. From there you can turn warmup on or off per inbox.

## Start warmup

1. Go to **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. Find the inbox that shows **Warm up required**, **Not started**, or **Start warmup**.
3. Click **Start**, **Enable warmup**, or the equivalent button for that inbox.
4. Warmup will begin. The inbox status in **Inbox Accounts** may change to **Warming**, and the Warmup page will show progress (e.g. a timeline or percentage).

## Pause warmup

1. Go to **Warmup**.
2. Find the inbox that is currently warming.
3. Click **Pause** (or **Pause warmup**) for that inbox.
4. Warmup stops; the inbox may show as **Paused**. You can resume later when you are ready.

## Resume warmup

1. Go to **Warmup**.
2. Find the inbox that shows **Paused** or **Resume warmup**.
3. Click **Resume** (or **Resume warmup**).
4. Warmup continues from where it left off. Progress will update again on the Warmup page and in Inbox Accounts.

## What happens when warmup runs

- Pigeon sends a controlled volume of emails from that inbox over time to build reputation.
- You do not need to run campaigns from that inbox during warmup; the warmup process runs in the background.
- Once the inbox reaches the target warmup level, its status in **Inbox Accounts** will show **Ready** (or similar), and you can safely use it for campaigns.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Warmup → find inbox → Start to begin warmup.
- [ ] Warmup → find inbox → Pause to stop warmup.
- [ ] Warmup → find inbox → Resume to continue after pausing.
excerpt: Use the Warmup page to start warmup for new inboxes, pause it when needed, and resume it later—all from one place.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Check Warmup Progress and When Your Inbox Is Ready
content:
## Where to see warmup progress

Warmup progress is visible in two places: the **Warmup** page (sidebar) and the **Inbox Accounts** page. The Warmup page shows a timeline or chart and per-inbox progress; Inbox Accounts shows a short status and often a percentage or "Warmed" label per inbox.

## On the Warmup page

1. Go to **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. You will see each inbox (Gmail and SMTP) that has warmup enabled.
3. For each inbox, look for:
   - **Progress** — e.g. a percentage (e.g. 45% warmed) or a progress bar.
   - **Timeline** — A chart showing how sending has increased over time.
   - **Status** — Warming, Paused, or Complete/Ready.
4. When the progress reaches the target (often 100% or the plan’s threshold), the inbox is considered ready. Its status in **Inbox Accounts** will typically change to **Ready**.

## On Inbox Accounts

1. Go to **Inbox Accounts** in the sidebar.
2. Each inbox row shows a **status** badge (Ready, Warming, Warm up required, Warning, Paused) and often a **warmup** value (e.g. "65% warmed" or "Warmed").
3. **Ready** (and sometimes a high warmup %) means you can use that inbox for campaigns within your plan limits. **Warming** means use only within the suggested warmup limits.

## When is my inbox ready?

- **Ready** — Safe to use for full campaign volume (within your daily and plan limits).
- **Warming** with a high percentage — Often you can start using it at reduced volume; check any in-app notes for recommended limits.
- **Warm up required** or **Warning** — Not ready; keep warmup running or fix the issue before sending campaigns from that inbox.

## Summary

Check **Warmup** for detailed progress and **Inbox Accounts** for a quick status. Use an inbox for campaigns when it shows **Ready** (or when warming limits allow).
excerpt: See warmup progress on the Warmup page and Inbox Accounts; use an inbox for campaigns when it shows Ready or within warming limits.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Import Contacts from CSV or Excel
content:
## Why import contacts?

Campaigns in Pigeon are sent to **contact lists**. You can build those lists by importing contacts from a CSV or Excel file (e.g. from your CRM or a spreadsheet). Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar, then use **Import** to upload your file and map columns to Pigeon fields.

## Step 1: Prepare your file

1. Your file should have one row per contact and columns for email and any other fields you need (e.g. first name, last name, company).
2. **Email** is required; other columns are optional. Supported formats: **.csv**, **.xlsx**, **.xls**. Maximum file size is typically 10 MB.
3. If you are unsure of the format, use **Contacts → Import** and download the **example CSV** from the import page to see the recommended structure.

## Step 2: Start the import

1. In Pigeon, go to **Contacts** (sidebar).
2. Click **Import** (or **Import contacts**).
3. Choose **Upload file** and select your CSV or Excel file, or drag and drop it. The app will read the first rows and show you the detected columns.

## Step 3: Map columns

1. You will see a **mapping** step: your file’s column headers on one side and Pigeon fields (e.g. Email, First name, Last name, Company, Industry, Location) on the other.
2. For each Pigeon field, select which column from your file should map to it (or leave blank to skip). **Email** must be mapped.
3. Confirm and continue. You may be asked whether to add contacts to an **existing list** or create a **new list**; choose one and give the new list a name if needed.

## Step 4: Save and review

1. Click **Import** or **Save**. Pigeon will process the file and add the contacts to the selected list.
2. You may see a summary (e.g. how many imported, any errors). Fix any errors (e.g. invalid emails) in your file and re-import if needed.
3. The new or updated list appears under **Contacts**. You can now select this list when creating a campaign.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Prepare CSV/Excel with at least an email column; max 10 MB.
- [ ] Contacts → Import → upload file.
- [ ] Map file columns to Pigeon fields (Email required).
- [ ] Choose existing list or new list → Import/Save.
- [ ] Use the list in Campaigns when creating a campaign.
excerpt: Upload a CSV or Excel file from Contacts → Import, map columns to Pigeon fields (email required), then add contacts to an existing or new list.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Map Columns When Importing Contacts
content:
## What is column mapping?

When you import contacts from a CSV or Excel file, **column mapping** tells Pigeon which column in your file corresponds to which contact field (e.g. Email, First name, Company). Your file might use headers like "Email Address" or "E-mail"; mapping links those to Pigeon’s **Email** field so contacts are imported correctly.

## Where mapping happens

After you upload a file in **Contacts → Import**, Pigeon shows a **mapping** step. You will see your file’s column names (from the first row) and a dropdown or list of Pigeon fields for each.

## Pigeon contact fields

Common fields you can map to include:
- **Email** (required) — The contact’s email address.
- **First name** — First name.
- **Last name** — Last name.
- **Company** — Company name.
- **Industry** — Industry or vertical.
- **Location** — Location or region.

You do not have to map every field; only **Email** is required. Map only the columns you have and care about.

## How to map

1. For **Email**, choose the column that contains email addresses (e.g. "Email", "E-mail", "Email Address"). This mapping is required.
2. For **First name**, select the column with first names, or leave unmapped if you don’t have it.
3. Repeat for **Last name**, **Company**, **Industry**, **Location** as needed.
4. If your file has columns that don’t match any Pigeon field, leave them unmapped; they won’t be imported.
5. Double-check that Email is correct—wrong mapping can cause imports to fail or create bad data.
6. Continue to the next step (e.g. choose list, then Import).

## Tips

- Use the **example CSV** on the import page to see recommended column names.
- Headers are usually taken from the first row; ensure the first row contains column names, not data.
- If you map the same file column to more than one Pigeon field, the last mapping usually wins; keep each field mapped to at most one column.

## Summary

Mapping links your file’s columns to Pigeon fields. Always map **Email**; map First name, Last name, Company, etc. only if your file has those columns.
excerpt: When importing contacts, map your file columns to Pigeon fields (Email required); map First name, Company, etc. where your file has them.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Create and Manage Contact Lists
content:
## What are contact lists?

In Pigeon, **contact lists** are the groups of contacts you send campaigns to. When you create a campaign, you choose one (or more) contact lists as the audience. You create lists by importing contacts (Contacts → Import) or by building them over time; you can have multiple lists and use different ones for different campaigns.

## Where to see and manage lists

1. Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar.
2. You may see **All Contacts** or a list of **Contact lists** (e.g. "Q1 Leads", "Newsletter"). Each list has a name and usually a count of contacts.
3. Click a list to view or edit its contacts, or use the options to rename, delete, or duplicate the list if your plan supports it.

## Creating a new list

**By import:**
1. **Contacts** → **Import**.
2. Upload your CSV/Excel file and map columns.
3. When asked "Add to existing list or new list", choose **Create new list** and enter a name (e.g. "Webinar signups").
4. Complete the import. The new list appears under Contacts.

**Empty list (if supported):**
- Some plans let you create an empty list from Contacts, then add contacts later (e.g. by import or manual add). Look for **New list** or **Create list** on the Contacts page.

## Managing lists

- **Rename** — Open the list or use a list menu and choose Rename; enter the new name.
- **Add contacts** — Import another file and choose "Add to existing list" and select this list; or add contacts manually if the option exists.
- **Remove contacts** — Edit the list and remove or delete individual contacts, or use filters/segments if available.
- **Delete list** — Use Delete or Remove list from the list’s menu. This usually removes the list and may affect campaigns that use it; update those campaigns if needed.
- **Duplicate** — If available, duplicate the list to create a copy with a new name.

## Using lists in campaigns

When you create or edit a campaign (**Campaigns** → New or Edit), in the audience/recipients step you select one or more **contact lists**. Only contacts in the selected list(s) will receive that campaign. You can change the list before launching; after launch, the campaign is tied to the list you chose.

## Summary

Contact lists hold your recipients. Create them via Import (new list or add to existing), manage them from Contacts, and select the right list when creating a campaign.
excerpt: Create contact lists by importing contacts (new or existing list), manage and rename them from Contacts, and choose the right list when creating campaigns.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Manually Block or Unblock Contacts
content:
## Why block or unblock contacts?

You may want to **block** a contact so they never receive campaigns from you (e.g. unsubscribes, invalid addresses, or people who asked to be removed). **Unblocking** lets you add them back to the pool so they can receive campaigns again. Pigeon has a **Manual Block / Unblock** area under **Contacts** for this.

## Where to block or unblock

1. Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar.
2. Open **Manual Block / Unblock** (it may be under a submenu or tab under Contacts).
3. You will see options to block or unblock contacts, often by entering an email or selecting from a list.

## Block a contact

1. In **Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock**, find the **Block** section or form.
2. Enter the **email address** of the contact you want to block (or select them from a list if the UI allows).
3. Confirm or click **Block**. The contact is added to the block list and will not receive future campaigns (and may be excluded from existing campaigns depending on how sends are processed).

## Unblock a contact

1. In **Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock**, find the **Unblock** section or list of blocked contacts.
2. Find the contact (e.g. by email) in the blocked list.
3. Click **Unblock** or **Remove from block list**. The contact is no longer blocked and can receive campaigns again if they are in a contact list you use.

## Viewing blocked contacts

- The Manual Block / Unblock page usually shows a list of currently blocked emails (or a way to search them). Use this to review who is blocked and to unblock if needed.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock.
- [ ] Block: enter email (or select) → Block.
- [ ] Unblock: find contact in blocked list → Unblock.
excerpt: Use Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock to block contacts so they don't receive campaigns and to unblock them when you want to send again.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Use Verified Leads (Pro)
content:
## What are Verified Leads?

**Verified Leads** is a Pro feature that helps you focus on contacts whose email addresses have been verified (e.g. through a double opt-in or verification step). This can improve deliverability and engagement by ensuring you are sending to valid, engaged addresses. The feature is available under **Contacts** when you are on a plan that includes it.

## Where to find Verified Leads

1. Go to **Contacts** in the sidebar.
2. Click **Verified Leads** (it may be under a submenu like "Contacts → Verified Leads").
3. You will see a list or view of contacts that are marked as verified.

## How verified leads work

- Contacts can be marked as **verified** when they confirm their email (e.g. by clicking a link in a verification email) or through another verification flow your process uses.
- The Verified Leads view filters or highlights these contacts so you can build lists or segments from them.
- When creating campaigns, you can target a contact list that contains only (or mostly) verified leads for better deliverability.

## Using verified leads in campaigns

1. Ensure you have contacts in the verified leads list (verification may happen when they sign up or when you run a verification step).
2. Create a **contact list** that includes your verified leads, or use a list that is built from the verified-leads data.
3. When creating a campaign, select that list as the audience. This way you send primarily to verified addresses.

## Summary

Verified Leads (Pro) surfaces contacts with verified emails. Use the Verified Leads view under Contacts to see and manage them, and use lists built from verified leads when creating campaigns for better results.
excerpt: Verified Leads (Pro) shows contacts with verified emails; use this view under Contacts and target verified leads in campaigns for better deliverability.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Create Your First Email Template
content:
## What are email templates?

**Email templates** in Pigeon are reusable email designs you use in campaigns. Each template has a **subject** and a **body** (and optionally a name). You can use **merge variables** (e.g. {{first_name}}, {{company}}) so each recipient gets a personalized message. Create and manage templates under **Templates** in the sidebar.

## Step 1: Open Templates

1. Click **Templates** in the sidebar.
2. Go to **Template Management** (or the main templates list).
3. Click **New template** or **Create template**.

## Step 2: Name and subject

1. Give the template a **name** (e.g. "Cold outreach – intro") so you can find it later.
2. Enter the **subject line**. You can use merge variables here too (e.g. "Hi {{first_name}}, quick question").

## Step 3: Write the body

1. In the **body** editor, write your email content. You can use plain text or HTML depending on what the editor supports.
2. Use **merge variables** where you want personalization: {{first_name}}, {{last_name}}, {{company}}, {{email}}, etc. These are replaced with the contact’s data when the campaign runs.
3. Include an **unsubscribe** line for compliance (e.g. "Unsubscribe: {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}" or the placeholder your plan uses). See the Compliance settings and template guide for the exact placeholder.
4. Save the template.

## Step 4: Use the template in a campaign

1. Go to **Campaigns** → **New campaign** (or edit an existing one).
2. In the email sequence step, add an email and select your new template from the template list.
3. The campaign will use this template for that step; merge variables will be filled from the contact list you choose.

## Tips

- Use **Templates → Template Guide** and **Template Examples** for suggested merge variables and best practices.
- Keep subject lines clear and avoid spammy words; check **Settings → Compliance** for spam words to avoid.
- Test with a small list or a test send if your plan supports it.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Templates → New template.
- [ ] Enter name, subject, and body; add merge variables and unsubscribe.
- [ ] Save; use the template in a campaign.
excerpt: Create a template from Templates → New template: add name, subject, body, merge variables, and an unsubscribe line, then use it in a campaign.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Use Merge Variables (first_name, company)
content:
## What are merge variables?

**Merge variables** are placeholders in your email templates that are replaced with each contact’s data when the campaign runs. For example, {{first_name}} becomes "John" for one contact and "Jane" for another. This personalization improves open and reply rates. The variables available depend on the **contact list** you use: they come from the fields in that list (e.g. from your import or CRM).

## Common merge variables

- **{{first_name}}** — First name
- **{{last_name}}** — Last name
- **{{email}}** — Email address
- **{{company}}** — Company name
- **{{industry}}** — Industry (if you have this field)
- **{{location}}** — Location (if you have this field)

Your list may have more custom fields; the **Template Guide** or **Template Prompts** under **Templates** often list the exact variables for the list you select in a campaign.

## Where to use them

- **Subject line** — e.g. "Hi {{first_name}}, one question about {{company}}".
- **Body** — e.g. "Hi {{first_name}}," or "I saw that {{company}} is in {{industry}}."
- Use only variables that exist on your contact list; if a field is missing for a contact, the placeholder might show blank or a default.

## How to insert merge variables

1. When editing a template (**Templates** → select template or New), type the variable name in double curly braces: {{first_name}}, {{company}}, etc.
2. Or use the template editor’s insert/list option if it shows available merge variables (e.g. from the selected contact list).
3. For **AI Campaign Studio** or campaign flows that use a list, the available variables are usually those in that list’s fields.

## Spintax (optional)

Some plans support **spintax** for variation: {Option A|Option B|Option C} randomly picks one option per email. Example: "Hi {Hi|Hello|Hey} {{first_name}}," — each recipient gets one of Hi, Hello, or Hey. Check the Template Guide for spintax syntax.

## Summary

Merge variables = {{field_name}}. Use {{first_name}}, {{company}}, etc. in subject and body; ensure your contact list has those fields. Check Templates → Template Guide for the full list.
excerpt: Use merge variables like {{first_name}} and {{company}} in templates; they are replaced with each contact's data from your list. Check the Template Guide for the full list.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Use the Template Guide and Examples
content:
## What are the Template Guide and Examples?

Pigeon provides a **Template Guide** and **Template Examples** under **Templates** to help you write better emails and use the right merge variables and placeholders. The Guide explains how templates work; the Examples show sample templates you can copy or adapt.

## Where to find them

1. Click **Templates** in the sidebar.
2. You will see sub-items such as **Template Management**, **Template Guide**, **Template Examples**, and **Template Prompts**.
3. Open **Template Guide** for documentation and **Template Examples** for sample emails.

## Using the Template Guide

- **Merge variables** — Lists the variables you can use (e.g. {{first_name}}, {{company}}) and where they come from (your contact list fields).
- **Unsubscribe** — How to add the unsubscribe link placeholder so your emails stay compliant (e.g. {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}} or the exact string for your plan).
- **Spintax** — If supported, how to use {Option A|Option B} for random variation per email.
- **Compliance** — Reminders about spam words, link limits, and image limits from Settings → Compliance.
- **Best practices** — Tips for subject lines, body length, and avoiding spam filters.

Use the Guide when creating or editing a template so you use the correct syntax and stay within compliance.

## Using Template Examples

- **Template Examples** shows pre-written example templates (e.g. cold outreach, follow-up, newsletter).
- You can **copy** an example into a new template and then edit the subject, body, and variables to match your campaign.
- Examples often include merge variables and an unsubscribe line; adjust them to your contact list and compliance settings.

## Template Prompts

**Template Prompts** (if available) may offer prompt ideas or suggestions for AI-generated templates when you use **AI Campaign Studio**. Check that page for prompts you can use to generate templates.

## Summary

Use **Templates → Template Guide** for merge variables, unsubscribe, and compliance; use **Template Examples** to copy and adapt sample templates for your campaigns.
excerpt: Use Templates → Template Guide for merge variables and compliance; use Template Examples to copy and adapt sample templates for your campaigns.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Add an Unsubscribe Link for Compliance
content:
## Why include an unsubscribe link?

Including a way for recipients to **unsubscribe** is required for compliance (e.g. CAN-SPAM, GDPR) and reduces spam complaints. Pigeon lets you add an **unsubscribe link** placeholder in your templates; when the campaign runs, it is replaced with a real link that lets contacts opt out. You can also enforce this in **Settings → Compliance**.

## Add the placeholder in your template

1. Go to **Templates** → create or edit a template.
2. In the **body** of the email, add a line such as:
   - "Unsubscribe: {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}" or
   - "To stop receiving these emails, unsubscribe here: {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}"
3. The exact placeholder name may vary by plan; check **Templates → Template Guide** for the correct placeholder (e.g. {{unsubscribe_url}} or {{insert-unsubscribe-link-here}}).
4. Save the template. When you use this template in a campaign, Pigeon will replace the placeholder with the working unsubscribe link.

## Enable "require unsubscribe" in Compliance

1. Go to **Settings** (sidebar) → **Compliance** tab.
2. Find the option **Require unsubscribe link** (or similar).
3. Turn it **on** so that templates or campaigns without an unsubscribe link are blocked or warned.
4. Save. This helps ensure every campaign stays compliant.

## Where to place the link

- Usually at the **bottom** of the email body (e.g. after your signature).
- Use clear wording: "Unsubscribe", "Manage preferences", or "Stop receiving these emails" with the link.
- One unsubscribe link per email is typically enough; avoid hiding it or using tiny font.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] In the template body, add the unsubscribe placeholder (see Template Guide for exact name).
- [ ] Settings → Compliance → Require unsubscribe link = On.
- [ ] Place the link at the bottom with clear text.
excerpt: Add the unsubscribe link placeholder in your template body (see Template Guide for exact name) and turn on Require unsubscribe in Settings → Compliance.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Create Your First Campaign in Pigeon
content:
## What is a campaign?

A **campaign** in Pigeon is an outreach sequence: you choose a **contact list**, one or more **email templates** (with optional delays between steps), and **sending inboxes** (Gmail or SMTP). Pigeon sends the emails according to your schedule and daily limits. Create campaigns from **Campaigns** in the sidebar.

## Before you start

- At least one **contact list** with contacts (Contacts → Import or create list).
- At least one **email template** (Templates → create with subject, body, merge variables, unsubscribe).
- At least one **inbox** ready to send (Gmail or SMTP in Inbox Accounts, status Ready or within warmup limits).

## Step 1: Start a new campaign

1. Go to **Campaigns** (sidebar).
2. Click **New campaign** or **Create campaign**.

## Step 2: Campaign info and audience

1. Enter a **campaign name** (e.g. "Q1 cold outreach").
2. Select the **contact list** (audience) for this campaign. Only contacts in this list will receive the emails.
3. Set **timezone** for send times (e.g. America/New_York).

## Step 3: Sender (inboxes)

1. Choose **Gmail** or **SMTP** as the sender type.
2. Select one or more **inboxes** from the list. These must be in Ready (or allowed) status.
3. Optionally set **sender rotation** (e.g. round-robin or random) if you have multiple inboxes.

## Step 4: Email sequence

1. Add one or more **steps** (emails). For each step, select a **template** and set a **delay** (e.g. 0 days for the first, 2 days for the second).
2. The first email is sent when the campaign runs; follow-ups are sent after the delay. Ensure all steps have a template selected.

## Step 5: Schedule and limits

1. Set **daily limit** (e.g. 50 emails per day across the campaign).
2. Set **send time window** (e.g. 9:00–17:00) so emails go out only in that range.
3. Optionally set **reply-to** (default from Settings or a specific Gmail/IMAP).

## Step 6: Launch

1. Review the summary and click **Launch** or **Start campaign**. The campaign will start sending according to your schedule and limits.
2. You can monitor progress under **Campaigns** (e.g. sent count, replies) and in **Inbox** for replies.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Campaigns → New campaign.
- [ ] Name, contact list, timezone.
- [ ] Gmail or SMTP + select inbox(es).
- [ ] Add sequence steps (template + delay per step).
- [ ] Daily limit and send time window.
- [ ] Launch.
excerpt: Create a campaign: name, contact list, Gmail or SMTP inboxes, email sequence (templates + delays), daily limit and send window, then launch.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Choose Gmail vs SMTP and Select Sending Inboxes
content:
## Gmail vs SMTP

When creating or editing a campaign, you choose how to send: **Gmail** (accounts you connected in Settings → Integrations) or **SMTP** (domain inboxes you added in Inbox Accounts after verifying your domain).

**Gmail** — Quick to set up; good for personal or small-team outreach. You connect Gmail via OAuth or App Password in Settings → Integrations → Gmail. Each connected account appears as an inbox you can select in the campaign.

**SMTP** — Send from your own domain (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com). You must verify the domain in **Domains** and add SMTP inboxes in **Inbox Accounts**. Then you can select those inboxes when the sender type is SMTP.

## How to choose in a campaign

1. Open **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** an existing one.
2. Find the **Sender** or **Sending from** section.
3. Select **Gmail** or **SMTP**:
   - **Gmail** — The list shows all Gmail accounts you connected. Select one or more; the campaign will send from these (with rotation if multiple).
   - **SMTP** — You may need to select a **domain** first; then select one or more SMTP inboxes for that domain. Only inboxes in **Ready** (or allowed) status should be used.
4. If you have multiple inboxes, set **sender rotation** (e.g. round-robin or random) so sends are spread across them.

## Tips

- Use **Ready** inboxes; avoid **Warm up required** or **Warning** unless you stay within warmup limits.
- For small lists, using fewer inboxes can be better for reputation; for large lists, spreading across more inboxes helps with daily limits.
- You can run a **test send** (if the campaign form has it) to confirm the selected inbox works before launching.
excerpt: In a campaign, choose Gmail (connected in Settings) or SMTP (domain inboxes from Inbox Accounts), then select one or more inboxes and set rotation if needed.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Set Daily Limits and Send Time Windows
content:
## Why set limits and send times?

**Daily limits** cap how many emails a campaign sends per day so you don’t overload your inbox reputation or hit provider limits. **Send time windows** (e.g. 9:00–17:00) ensure emails go out only during business hours in the recipient’s timezone, which can improve opens and replies. You set both when creating or editing a campaign.

## Where to set them

1. Go to **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** an existing campaign.
2. Find the **Schedule**, **Sending**, or **Limits** section (often after you choose contact list and inboxes).

## Daily limit

1. **Daily limit** — Enter the maximum number of emails this campaign can send per day (e.g. 50 or 100). The campaign will stop sending for the day once this number is reached and continue the next day.
2. This limit usually applies to the campaign as a whole (across all selected inboxes). Keep it within your plan and warmup recommendations.

## Send time window

1. **Start time** and **End time** — Set the window when emails can be sent (e.g. 09:00 to 17:00). Only contacts whose local time falls in this window will receive emails at that time.
2. **Timezone** — Set the campaign timezone (e.g. America/New_York). Pigeon uses this (and the contact’s timezone if available) to send within the window.
3. Sends are typically spread across the window rather than all at once, depending on your plan.

## Best practices

- Start with a conservative daily limit (e.g. 30–50) for new inboxes; increase as reputation builds.
- Use business-hour windows (e.g. 8–18) in the recipient’s region to improve engagement.
- If you have a "best send time" or analytics suggestion in the campaign form, consider using it.

## Summary

Set **daily limit** and **start/end time** (and **timezone**) in the campaign form so sends are capped and only go out during your chosen window.
excerpt: In the campaign form set a daily limit and a send time window (start/end time + timezone) so sends are capped and only during business hours.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Use AI to Generate Campaign Templates (AI Campaign Studio)
content:
## What is AI Campaign Studio?

**AI Campaign Studio** in Pigeon lets you generate email templates using AI. You describe what you want (e.g. "cold outreach to SaaS founders"), pick a contact list (so the AI uses the right merge variables), and the AI suggests subject and body. You can then edit the result and use it in a campaign or save it as a template. Open it from **AI Campaign Studio** in the sidebar.

## Step 1: Open AI Campaign Studio

1. Click **AI Campaign Studio** in the sidebar.
2. You may see a chat-style interface or a form where you describe your campaign and select a list.

## Step 2: Describe your campaign and select list

1. Enter a **prompt** or description: e.g. "Write a short cold email for B2B SaaS founders, focus on time savings."
2. Select the **contact list** you will use for this campaign. The AI will use only merge variables that exist on that list (e.g. {{first_name}}, {{company}}).
3. If there is an option to choose an **AI provider** (e.g. OpenAI), select one that is configured in Settings → Integrations.

## Step 3: Generate and edit

1. Click **Generate** or **Create**. The AI will produce a template (name, subject, body) with merge variables and optionally an unsubscribe line.
2. Review and **edit** the subject and body in the editor. You can change wording, add spintax, or adjust the unsubscribe line to match your Compliance settings.
3. Run **compliance check** if the tool offers it (e.g. spam words, link count) and fix any issues.

## Step 4: Use the template

1. **Save as template** — Save the generated email as a new template in **Templates** so you can reuse it in any campaign.
2. **Use in campaign** — You may be able to start a campaign from AI Campaign Studio using this template and the same contact list; or go to **Campaigns** → New campaign and select the saved template in the sequence.

## Tips

- Use **Templates → Template Prompts** for prompt ideas.
- Always include an unsubscribe line and stay within Compliance (spam words, links, images).
- Generate once, then tweak for your brand and list.

## Summary

AI Campaign Studio: describe your email, select contact list, generate → edit → save as template or use in a campaign.

title: How to Run Template A/B Tests in a Campaign
content:
## What is template A/B testing?

**A/B testing** in a campaign means sending two (or more) versions of an email (e.g. different subject lines or bodies) to parts of your audience and comparing performance (opens, replies). Pigeon supports this so you can see which template performs better. The exact controls depend on your plan; look for **A/B test** or **Template A/B Testing** when creating or editing a campaign or a sequence step.

## Where to set it up

1. Go to **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** a campaign.
2. In the **email sequence** section, when you add or edit a step, look for **A/B test** or **Variants** (e.g. "Add variant" or "Test subject A vs B").
3. You may also see A/B options under **Get Started** (sidebar) in the "Template A/B Testing" section as part of the product tour.

## How to run an A/B test

1. For the step you want to test, add **two (or more) variants**: e.g. Template A (subject line A) and Template B (subject line B), or two different templates.
2. Set the **split** (e.g. 50% / 50%) so part of the audience gets variant A and part gets variant B.
3. Launch the campaign. Pigeon will send the variants according to the split.
4. After sends, check **Analytics** or **Campaign** stats to compare opens, replies, or other metrics for each variant. The better-performing variant can inform future templates.

## Best practices

- Test one thing at a time (e.g. subject line only, or body only) so results are clear.
- Use a large enough audience so the split gives meaningful numbers.
- Run the test for a set period or until you have enough data, then use the winner for future campaigns.

## Summary

Add A/B variants to a campaign step (templates or subjects), set the split, launch, and compare performance in Analytics to improve your templates.
excerpt: Add A/B variants (e.g. two templates or subjects) to a campaign step, set the split, launch, and compare performance in Analytics.

title: How to Edit or Pause a Campaign
content:
## Editing a campaign

You can **edit** a campaign to change its name, contact list, inboxes, email sequence, daily limit, send times, or reply-to—depending on your plan and whether the campaign has started. Some changes may only apply to future sends.

1. Go to **Campaigns** in the sidebar.
2. Find the campaign in the list and click it (or click **Edit**).
3. Change the fields you need (name, list, inboxes, sequence, limits, etc.).
4. **Save** or **Update**. If the campaign is already running, confirm whether changes apply to the next batch or only to new campaigns; the UI will guide you.

## Pausing a campaign

1. Go to **Campaigns**.
2. Find the campaign that is **running** or **active**.
3. Click **Pause** (or the pause icon/button). Confirm if asked.
4. The campaign stops sending. Recipients who already received some emails will not get the remaining steps until you resume.

## Resuming a paused campaign

1. In **Campaigns**, find the campaign with status **Paused**.
2. Click **Resume** (or the play/resume button).
3. The campaign continues from where it left off (e.g. follow-up emails will go out according to delays and limits).

## What you can and cannot change

- **Before launch** — You can usually change everything.
- **After launch** — You can often still change daily limit, send window, or pause/resume; changing the contact list or sequence might affect only future sends or require care. Follow the in-app warnings.

## Summary

**Edit**: Campaigns → select campaign → Edit → change fields → Save. **Pause**: Campaigns → select running campaign → Pause. **Resume**: Campaigns → select paused campaign → Resume.
excerpt: Edit a campaign from Campaigns → select → Edit; pause a running campaign with Pause, and resume a paused one with Resume.

title: How to View and Manage Campaign Replies in the Inbox
content:
## What is the Inbox?

The **Inbox** in Pigeon is where you see **replies** to your campaign emails. When a contact replies to a message sent from a campaign, that reply can appear in the Inbox so you can read it, mark it read, and follow up. The Inbox may also show an unread count in the sidebar.

## Where to open the Inbox

1. Click **Inbox** in the sidebar (sometimes labeled "Inbox" or "Campaign replies").
2. You will see a list of replies (or threads) from contacts, often with the contact’s name/email, subject, snippet, and date.

## Viewing replies

1. Each row is usually one reply (or thread). Click a reply to open it and read the full message.
2. You may see which **campaign** and **contact** the reply is from, and the original email you sent.
3. Mark replies as **read** or **unread** so you can track what still needs a response.

## Managing replies

- **Read / Unread** — Toggle read status so you can prioritize.
- **Filter or search** — If the Inbox has filters (e.g. by campaign, date), use them to find specific replies.
- **Reply in your own email** — Often you answer the contact in your normal email client (Gmail, Outlook) using the reply-to address you set for the campaign. Pigeon’s Inbox is for **viewing** campaign replies in one place; replying is typically done in your mailbox.

## Why replies appear here

Replies are collected because you connected Gmail or Reply-To IMAP in **Settings → Integrations** and set the campaign’s reply-to to an address Pigeon monitors. Ensure reply-to is set correctly so campaign replies show up in the Inbox.

## Summary

Open **Inbox** from the sidebar to view and manage campaign replies; mark read/unread and use filters. Reply to contacts in your own email client.
excerpt: Open Inbox from the sidebar to view campaign replies, mark them read/unread, and use filters; reply to contacts in your own email client.
author: Pigeon Team

title: How to Use the Inbox to See When Contacts Respond
content:
## Why use the Inbox for responses?

When contacts **respond** to your campaign emails, their replies need to be seen and answered quickly. Pigeon’s **Inbox** aggregates those replies in one place so you don’t have to check each sending inbox separately. You can see when someone responded, which campaign and contact they’re from, and then reply from your own email.

## See new responses

1. Click **Inbox** in the sidebar. The badge or label may show an **unread** count.
2. New replies appear in the list (newest first or by date, depending on the UI). Each entry usually shows: contact name/email, subject or snippet, campaign name, and time.
3. Open a reply to read the full message and the thread context (what you sent, what they replied).

## Stay on top of replies

- **Notifications** — Turn on **Settings → Notifications** for reply notifications so you get an email or in-app alert when someone responds.
- **Mark as read** — After handling a reply, mark it read so the unread count stays accurate.
- **Check regularly** — Use the Inbox as your single place to see all campaign replies so you can respond in a timely way.

## Replying to contacts

- Pigeon’s Inbox is for **viewing** replies. To **reply** to the contact, use your normal email client (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) and reply to the address that received their message (the reply-to address you set for the campaign). That keeps the thread in your mailbox.
- If you use **Tickets** or a linked support tool, you may be able to handle conversations there; check your plan and Settings.

## Summary

Use **Inbox** to see when contacts respond, read their messages, and mark them read; then reply from your email client. Enable reply notifications in Settings for faster follow-up.
excerpt: Use the Inbox to see when contacts respond, read replies, and mark them read; enable reply notifications in Settings and reply from your email client.

title: How to Read Your Dashboard and Analytics
content:
## Where to find Dashboard and Analytics

- **Dashboard** — Usually the first page after login; gives a high-level overview (e.g. sent today, replies, active campaigns, inbox status). Open it from **Dashboard** in the sidebar.
- **Analytics** — Deeper metrics: sends over time, opens, replies, breakdown by campaign or inbox. Open it from **Analytics** in the sidebar.

## What the Dashboard shows

- **Sent** — Emails sent today or this period.
- **Replies** — Number of replies (or unread replies).
- **Campaigns** — Active or recent campaigns and their status.
- **Inboxes** — Quick view of inbox status (Ready, Warming, etc.) or warmup progress.
- **Alerts** — Any deliverability or system alerts you should act on.

Use the Dashboard to see at a glance whether everything is running and whether you need to check Inbox, Campaigns, or Alerts.

## What Analytics shows

- **Timeline** — Sends (and sometimes opens/replies) over time (e.g. last 7 or 30 days).
- **By campaign** — Which campaigns sent how many emails and their performance.
- **By inbox** — Which inboxes sent how many; useful for balancing load and warmup.
- **Best send times** — If available, when your audience tends to open or reply.

Use Analytics to see trends, compare campaigns, and decide when to send and which inboxes to use.

## How to use them

- **Daily** — Check Dashboard for sent count, replies, and alerts.
- **Weekly** — Check Analytics for trends and campaign/inbox performance; adjust daily limits or send times if needed.
- **Before scaling** — Use Analytics to confirm inboxes and campaigns are healthy before increasing volume.

## Summary

**Dashboard** = quick overview (sent, replies, campaigns, inboxes, alerts). **Analytics** = detailed metrics over time and by campaign/inbox. Use both to monitor and improve performance.
excerpt: Dashboard gives a quick overview (sent, replies, campaigns, inboxes); Analytics shows detailed metrics over time and by campaign/inbox.

title: How to Use Sending Behavior (Tracking) to Improve Deliverability
content:
## What is Sending Behavior (Tracking)?

**Sending Behavior** (or **Tracking**) in Pigeon is the page that shows how you are sending over time: volume, distribution by hour, by inbox, and by campaign. It helps you spot patterns that can hurt deliverability (e.g. sending too much at once, or from one inbox only) and adjust so your emails are more likely to land in the inbox. Open it from **Sending Behavior** or **Tracking** in the sidebar.

## What you see

- **Charts** — Sends over time (e.g. last 7 days), often by day and by hour.
- **By inbox** — Which inboxes sent how many emails; balance sending across inboxes.
- **By campaign** — Which campaigns sent how many; avoid one campaign dominating.
- **Insights** — Some plans show tips (e.g. "Spread sends across more hours" or "Reduce peak rate").

## How to improve deliverability

1. **Spread sends** — If most emails go out in one hour, providers may treat it as bulk. Use **daily limit** and **send time window** in campaigns to spread sends across the day.
2. **Balance inboxes** — If one inbox sends much more than others, consider adding more inboxes or rotating senders so no single inbox is overloaded.
3. **Stay within warmup** — For warming inboxes, keep volume within the recommended limits shown in Warmup and Inbox Accounts.
4. **Use the data** — Check Sending Behavior regularly (e.g. weekly); if you see spikes or imbalance, adjust campaign limits or send windows.

## Summary

Use **Sending Behavior** (Tracking) to see send volume and distribution; spread sends over time and across inboxes to improve deliverability.
excerpt: Use Sending Behavior (Tracking) to see send volume and distribution; spread sends over time and across inboxes to improve deliverability.

title: How to Understand Sending by Inbox and by Campaign
content:
## Why sending by inbox and campaign matters

Seeing **sending by inbox** and **by campaign** helps you balance load (so no single inbox or campaign is overloaded), stay within warmup limits, and fix issues when one campaign or inbox underperforms. You can see this in **Analytics** and **Sending Behavior** (Tracking).

## Sending by inbox

- In **Sending Behavior** or **Analytics**, look for a breakdown **by inbox** (e.g. a chart or table: inbox A sent X, inbox B sent Y).
- **Use it to**: Balance volume across inboxes so no one inbox sends too much; check that warming inboxes stay within limits; see which inboxes are most used so you can add more if needed.

## Sending by campaign

- In **Analytics** or **Campaigns**, you can see per-campaign stats: how many emails each campaign sent, over what period, and sometimes opens/replies.
- **Use it to**: Compare campaign performance; see which campaigns are active and how much they send; pause or adjust campaigns that send too much or underperform.

## Where to find it

1. **Analytics** (sidebar) — Often has "By campaign" and "By inbox" views or filters.
2. **Sending Behavior** / **Tracking** (sidebar) — Shows send volume; switch or filter by inbox or campaign if the UI offers it.
3. **Campaigns** — Each campaign’s detail page may show sent count and basic stats.
4. **Inbox Accounts** — May show "sent today" per inbox.

## Summary

Use **Analytics** and **Sending Behavior** to see sending by inbox and by campaign; balance inbox usage and adjust campaigns for better deliverability and performance.
excerpt: Use Analytics and Sending Behavior to see sending by inbox and by campaign; balance volume and adjust campaigns for better deliverability.

title: How to Configure Compliance Settings (Spam Words, Links, Unsubscribe)
content:
## Why compliance settings matter

**Compliance** settings in Pigeon help you avoid spam triggers: banned words, too many links or images, and missing unsubscribe links. Configuring them reduces the chance your emails are filtered or flagged. Open **Settings** (sidebar) → **Compliance** tab.

## Spam words

1. In **Settings → Compliance**, find **Spam words** (or "Words to avoid").
2. Enter a list of words or phrases that often trigger spam filters (e.g. "free", "guarantee", "act now"). Separate with commas or new lines.
3. Save. Pigeon may warn or block templates that contain these words; fix templates and try again.

## Max links and images

1. Find **Max links per email** and **Max images per email** (e.g. 3 links, 2 images).
2. Set limits that match best practices (fewer links and images often perform better and look less like spam).
3. Save. Templates that exceed these limits may be rejected or flagged.

## Require unsubscribe link

1. Find **Require unsubscribe link** (or similar).
2. Turn it **on** so that every template (or campaign) must include the unsubscribe placeholder. This keeps you compliant with CAN-SPAM and similar rules.
3. Save.

## After changing compliance

- **Templates** — Review existing templates; remove spam words and add unsubscribe if required. Use **Templates → Template Guide** for the correct unsubscribe placeholder.
- **New campaigns** — New templates will be checked against these settings before save or launch.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] Settings → Compliance.
- [ ] Set spam words list; set max links and max images.
- [ ] Turn on "Require unsubscribe link".
- [ ] Update templates to match.
excerpt: In Settings → Compliance set spam words, max links and images, and require unsubscribe link; then update templates to match.

title: How to Set Up Notification Preferences for Replies
content:
## Why set reply notifications?

When contacts **reply** to your campaign emails, you want to know quickly so you can respond. Pigeon can send you **notifications** (e.g. by email to your account email) when a reply arrives. You control this in **Settings → Notifications**.

## Where to set them

1. Go to **Settings** (sidebar).
2. Open the **Notifications** tab.
3. Find **Notification Preferences** or **Reply notifications** (or similar).

## What you can turn on

- **Reply notifications** — When a contact replies to a campaign email, Pigeon can send you an email (to the address you signed up with) or show an in-app alert. Turn this **on** if you want to be notified for every reply, or **off** if you prefer to check the Inbox manually.
- Other notification types (e.g. campaign completed, alerts) may be listed; enable or disable each as you prefer.

## How notifications are sent

- Notifications are typically sent to your **account email** (the one you use to log in). Ensure that address is correct in **Settings → Account**.
- If you turn on reply notifications, you will get an email (or in-app notice) when a new reply appears in the Inbox; you can then open the Inbox and reply from your email client.

## Summary

**Settings → Notifications** → turn on **Reply notifications** (and any others you want) so you are notified when contacts respond. Notifications go to your account email.

title: How to Manage Security and Active Sessions
content:
## Where to manage security and sessions

You can review **active sessions** (devices or browsers where you are logged in) and manage **security** (e.g. password) from **Settings**. Open **Settings** (sidebar) → **Security** tab.

## Active sessions

1. In **Settings → Security**, find **Active sessions** (or "Sessions").
2. You will see a list of sessions: device/browser, location (if available), and last active time.
3. **Current session** is usually marked (the one you are using now).
4. For any other session, you can click **Revoke** or **Log out** to end that session. The user will need to log in again on that device. Use this if you lost a device or see a session you don’t recognize.

## Password and account security

- **Change password** — If the option is available, use it to set a new password. Use a strong, unique password.
- **Account email** — Your login email is often shown in **Settings → Account**. Change it there if your plan allows; notifications and password reset go to that email.

## Best practices

- Revoke sessions you no longer use (e.g. old phones or shared computers).
- If you see an unknown session, revoke it and change your password.
- Keep your account email up to date so you receive security and reply notifications.

## Summary

**Settings → Security** → view **Active sessions**, revoke any you don’t recognize; change password and check account email as needed.

title: How to Update Billing and Subscription
content:

You can view your **subscription**, **plan**, and **billing details** (and update payment method or plan) from **Settings**. Open **Settings** (sidebar) → **Billing** tab.

**Settings → Billing** — View plan and subscription; update payment method; change, cancel, or pause plan as needed.
