title: Why Your Gmail Connection Fails and How to Fix It
content:
## Common reasons Gmail connection fails

When **Connect Gmail** or adding a Gmail account fails in Pigeon, it is usually due to credentials, security settings, or plan limits. Below are the most common causes and how to fix them.

## 1. Invalid credentials (App Password)

**Symptom**: "Invalid credentials" or "Authentication failed".

**Fix**:
- You must use an **App Password**, not your normal Gmail password. In Google Account → Security → 2-Step Verification → App passwords, generate a new App Password for Mail / Other (Pigeon) and paste it into Pigeon (Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect via App Password).
- Ensure 2-Step Verification is turned on; without it, App Passwords are not available.

## 2. Google OAuth credentials not set

**Symptom**: "Google OAuth credentials not set" or you cannot use "Connect with Google".

**Fix**: An admin must add **Google Client ID** and **Client Secret** in Pigeon (Settings → Integrations → Gmail). See our blog "How to Set Up Google Client ID and Secret for Gmail" for the full steps. After they are saved, try Connect with Google again.

## 3. Redirect URI mismatch (OAuth)

**Symptom**: After signing in with Google, you see "Redirect URI mismatch" or "Error 400".

**Fix**: In Google Cloud Console, the **Authorized redirect URI** for your OAuth client must match **exactly** the URI shown in Pigeon when you add credentials (Settings → Integrations → Gmail). Copy the URI from Pigeon and paste it into Google Cloud; do not type it by hand. Then try connecting again.

## 4. Plan limit reached

**Symptom**: "You have reached the Gmail limit for your plan" or similar.

**Fix**: Your plan allows only a certain number of Gmail accounts. Disconnect an unused Gmail in Settings → Integrations → Gmail, or upgrade your plan to add more.

## 5. App not verified (OAuth)

**Symptom**: Google shows "This app isn’t verified" when you try to sign in.

**Fix**: For testing, you can choose **Advanced** → **Go to Pigeon (unsafe)** to continue. For production, consider submitting your app for Google verification so the warning goes away.

## Summary

Check: App Password (not normal password) and 2-Step Verification; OAuth Client ID/Secret and redirect URI; plan Gmail limit; and app verification if using OAuth.
excerpt: Fix Gmail connection failures: use App Password and 2-Step Verification; set OAuth Client ID/Secret and redirect URI; check plan limits and app verification.

title: Redirect URI Mismatch: How to Fix Google OAuth Errors
content:
## What is redirect URI mismatch?

When you use **Connect with Google** (OAuth) in Pigeon, Google redirects the user back to your app after sign-in. The **redirect URI** is the URL Google sends them to. If that URL does not **exactly** match one of the **Authorized redirect URIs** in your Google Cloud OAuth client, Google shows an error (e.g. "Redirect URI mismatch" or "Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch").

## Why it happens

- The URI in Google Cloud was typed by hand and has a typo or wrong path.
- The URI in Google Cloud uses http instead of https (or the wrong domain/port).
- Pigeon’s callback URL changed (e.g. after a domain or config change) and Google was not updated.

## How to fix it

1. **Get the exact URI from Pigeon**
   - In Pigeon, go to **Settings** → **Integrations** → **Gmail**.
   - Open the form where you enter **Google Client ID** and **Client Secret** (or "Add your Google OAuth credentials").
   - On that page, Pigeon shows the **Authorized redirect URI** you must use. Copy it exactly (including https, domain, and path).

2. **Update Google Cloud Console**
   - Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) → **APIs & Services** → **Credentials**.
   - Click your **OAuth 2.0 Client ID** (Web application).
   - Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, add the URI you copied from Pigeon (or replace the wrong one). Do not add extra spaces or characters.
   - Save.

3. **Try again**
   - In Pigeon, click **Connect with Google** again. The sign-in and redirect should complete without the mismatch error.

## Important

- **Copy from Pigeon, don’t type.** The URI must match character for character.
- If you have multiple environments (e.g. staging vs production), each has its own redirect URI; add each one in Google Cloud if you use both.

## Summary

Copy the **Authorized redirect URI** from Pigeon (Settings → Integrations → Gmail, when adding credentials), paste it into your Google Cloud OAuth client’s Authorized redirect URIs, save, then try Connect with Google again.
excerpt: Copy the Authorized redirect URI from Pigeon (Settings → Integrations → Gmail), add it exactly in Google Cloud OAuth client, then try Connect with Google again.

title: Best Practices for Inbox Warmup Before Sending Campaigns
content:
## Why warmup before campaigns?

Sending a lot of email from a **new or cold inbox** can hurt deliverability: providers may treat it as spam. **Warmup** gradually builds sender reputation so your real campaigns are more likely to land in the inbox. Follow these practices for best results.

## Start warmup early

- Add new Gmail or SMTP inboxes in **Inbox Accounts**, then go to **Warmup** and **start warmup** for each new inbox.
- Do not launch large campaigns from an inbox that is still in **Warm up required** or early **Warming**. Wait until status is **Ready** (or follow the recommended limits for warming inboxes).

## Respect warmup limits

- While an inbox is **Warming**, Pigeon (or your plan) may suggest a maximum daily send. Stay at or below that so the warmup curve is not disrupted.
- Use **Inbox Accounts** and **Warmup** to see progress; only increase campaign volume when the inbox is ready.

## Use multiple inboxes wisely

- Spreading volume across several warmed inboxes is better than overloading one. Add more inboxes and use **sender rotation** in campaigns (round-robin or random).
- For small lists, using fewer inboxes can be easier to manage and still safe if they are fully warmed.

## Don’t pause and rush

- If you **pause** warmup, resume it when you are ready; don’t send at full volume as soon as you resume. Let warmup continue to **Ready** before scaling campaigns.
- Avoid sending big bursts from a single inbox; use **daily limits** and **send time windows** in campaigns to spread sends.

## Monitor and adjust

- Check **Sending Behavior** (Tracking) and **Analytics** to see send volume per inbox. If one inbox is sending much more than others, balance by adding more inboxes or adjusting campaign sender selection.
- If you get **Alerts** about deliverability or reputation, slow down or pause campaigns and ensure warmup is complete for the affected inboxes.

## Summary

Start warmup for new inboxes, wait until Ready (or within warming limits), respect daily limits, spread volume across inboxes, and monitor Sending Behavior and Alerts.
excerpt: Start warmup for new inboxes, wait until Ready or within limits, respect daily limits, spread volume across inboxes, and monitor Sending Behavior and Alerts.

title: How to Use the Get Started Checklist
content:
## What is the Get Started checklist?

The **Get Started** page in Pigeon is a guided checklist that walks you through the main steps to send your first campaign: domains, inboxes, warmup, contacts, templates, and campaigns. Use it when you are new or when you want to confirm you haven’t missed a step. Open it from **Get Started** in the sidebar.

## Where to find it

1. Click **Get Started** in the sidebar (often near the top or under a welcome section).
2. You will see sections such as: Before You Start, Domains, Inbox Accounts, Warmup, Contacts, Templates, Campaigns, A/B Testing, Inbox (Replies), Dashboard & Analytics, Alerts, Settings & Support, and a **Quick Start Checklist**.

## How to use it

1. **Work through the sections in order** — Each section explains what to do (e.g. add a domain, verify it, add inboxes, start warmup, import contacts, create a template, create a campaign).
2. **Use the links** — Get Started links to the right pages (Domains, Inbox Accounts, Contacts, Templates, Campaigns, Settings, etc.) so you can complete each step.
3. **Quick Start Checklist** — At the end, a checklist summarizes the main tasks. Tick them off as you go: domain verified, inbox(es) added and warmed, contacts imported, template created, campaign launched.

## When to use it

- **First time** — Follow Get Started from top to bottom to set up domains, inboxes, warmup, contacts, templates, and your first campaign.
- **Refresher** — If you add a new domain or inbox later, open Get Started and jump to the relevant section (e.g. Domains or Warmup).
- **Troubleshooting** — If something is missing (e.g. "No inboxes" when creating a campaign), the checklist reminds you what to set up first.

## Summary

**Get Started** in the sidebar is your step-by-step guide: domains → inboxes → warmup → contacts → templates → campaigns. Use the Quick Start Checklist to track progress.
excerpt: Use Get Started in the sidebar to follow the step-by-step guide (domains, inboxes, warmup, contacts, templates, campaigns) and the Quick Start Checklist.

title: Understanding Alerts: Deliverability and System Notifications
content:
## What are Alerts?

**Alerts** in Pigeon are notifications about **deliverability** and **system** issues: e.g. a domain or inbox problem, a campaign issue, or a recommendation to act. They help you fix problems before they affect your sending. Open **Alerts** from the sidebar.

## Where to see Alerts

1. Click **Alerts** in the sidebar.
2. You will see a list of alerts (often newest first). Each alert has a **type** (e.g. success, warning, error, info), a **message**, and a **date**.
3. Some alerts may show in the **Dashboard** or as a badge on the Alerts item in the sidebar (e.g. unread count).

## Types of alerts

- **Success** — Something completed successfully (e.g. domain verified, campaign finished).
- **Warning** — Something to watch (e.g. warmup progress low, high bounce rate).
- **Error** — Something failed or is broken (e.g. inbox connection failed, domain verification failed).
- **Info** — General information or tips.

## What to do when you get an alert

1. **Read the message** — It usually explains what happened and which resource is affected (e.g. domain, inbox, campaign).
2. **Take action** — For example: fix DNS if domain verification failed; reconnect or fix credentials if an inbox failed; pause a campaign or improve warmup if you see a deliverability warning.
3. **Mark as read** — Use **Mark as read** (if available) so you can track what you’ve handled. You can **delete** old alerts to keep the list clean.

## Deliverability vs system

- **Deliverability alerts** — Relate to domains, inboxes, warmup, bounces, or reputation. Act on these so your emails keep landing in the inbox.
- **System alerts** — Relate to the app (e.g. maintenance, feature changes). Read them for context; no action may be needed.

## Summary

**Alerts** (sidebar) shows deliverability and system notifications. Read each alert, take action when needed (e.g. fix domain, inbox, or warmup), and mark read or delete to stay on top of issues.
excerpt: Alerts show deliverability and system notifications; read them, fix issues (domain, inbox, warmup), and mark read or delete as needed.

title: Understanding Gmail Sending Limits: OAuth vs App Password
content:
## Why Gmail limits matter

Google applies **daily sending limits** to each Gmail account. If you exceed them, emails may bounce or your account can be restricted. Pigeon respects these limits so your campaigns run safely. The limit depends on **how** you connect: OAuth (sign-in with Google) or App Password.

## OAuth (Connect with Google) — ~500 per day

When you connect Gmail via **OAuth** (Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect with Google), you use the Gmail web/API channel. For **personal Gmail** (@gmail.com), Google typically allows around **500 recipients per day** per account. This is the higher limit and is best for outreach volume.

## App Password — ~100 per day

When you connect via **App Password** (Settings → Integrations → Gmail → Connect via App Password), Pigeon uses SMTP/IMAP. For personal Gmail, Google typically allows around **100 recipients per day** per account. Use this when you prefer not to use OAuth.

## What Pigeon does

- **Per-inbox limits** — You can set a daily limit per inbox in Pigeon (e.g. 50). We never send more than your configured limit or Google's cap.
- **New inboxes** — For inboxes newer than 7 days or near their daily cap, we use a safer sending pattern (see Sending Behavior / Sent tooltip).
- **Reset time** — Per-inbox limits reset at **midnight UTC**. Plan your campaign daily limits and send windows accordingly.

## Tips

- Prefer **OAuth** if your plan supports it for higher daily volume per Gmail.
- Use **multiple Gmail accounts** (within your plan limit) and spread volume across them.
- Start with a **low daily limit** (e.g. 50) and increase gradually; Google may adjust limits based on your sending behaviour.

## Summary

OAuth ≈ 500/day, App Password ≈ 100/day for personal Gmail. Pigeon enforces per-inbox limits and resets at midnight UTC; stay within both for best deliverability.
excerpt: Gmail limits: OAuth ~500/day, App Password ~100/day. How Pigeon respects them and resets at midnight UTC.

title: How to Create a Full Campaign with AI Campaign Studio (From Prompt to Launch)
content:
## What you can do in AI Campaign Studio

**AI Campaign Studio** lets you go from a short description to a **launched campaign** in one flow. You pick a contact list, describe your outreach (e.g. "cold outreach to SaaS founders about time savings"), and the AI generates templates and builds the campaign. You can then edit, set schedule and daily limit, and launch.

## Step 1: Open AI Campaign Studio

1. Click **AI Campaign Studio** in the sidebar.
2. You will see a chat-style interface or a form to describe your campaign.

## Step 2: Choose your audience

1. Select the **contact list** this campaign will use. The AI will use only merge variables that exist on that list (e.g. {{first_name}}, {{company}}).
2. If you need a new list, create it first under **Contacts** (e.g. import from CSV) and then come back.

## Step 3: Describe your campaign

1. Enter a **prompt** or description: e.g. "Cold email sequence for B2B SaaS founders, 3 steps: intro, value prop, soft CTA. Focus on saving time."
2. Optionally add **links to include** or **additional details** so the AI weaves them into the copy.
3. Click **Generate** or **Create campaign**. The AI will produce one or more email templates and a sequence (subject + body per step, with delays).

## Step 4: Review and edit

1. Review the generated **subject** and **body** for each step. Edit wording, merge variables, or add an unsubscribe line if needed.
2. Run a **compliance check** (spam words, link count) and fix any issues.
3. Confirm the **sequence order** and **delays** between steps.

## Step 5: Set schedule and daily limit

1. Set **timezone** and **send time window** (e.g. 9:00–17:00).
2. Set **daily limit** (e.g. 50 emails per day). The AI or form may suggest a default; keep it conservative for new inboxes.
3. Choose **sending inboxes** (Gmail or SMTP). Use only **Ready** (or allowed) inboxes.

## Step 6: Launch

1. Click **Launch** or **Start campaign**. Pigeon will create the campaign and start sending according to your schedule and limits.
2. Monitor progress under **Campaigns** and replies under **Inbox**.

## Summary checklist

- [ ] AI Campaign Studio → select contact list.
- [ ] Describe campaign (prompt + optional links/details) → Generate.
- [ ] Edit templates and sequence; run compliance check.
- [ ] Set timezone, send window, daily limit, inboxes.
- [ ] Launch and monitor in Campaigns and Inbox.
excerpt: Use AI Campaign Studio to go from a prompt to a launched campaign: pick list, describe intent, generate sequence, set schedule and daily limit, then launch.

title: AI Campaign Studio: Chat Commands to Create or Edit Campaigns
content:
## Using chat to control campaigns

In **AI Campaign Studio** you can use **natural language** to create a new campaign or to **edit** an existing one (e.g. change name, daily limit, timezone, or follow-up delay). The AI interprets your instruction and updates the campaign or creates it.

## Creating a campaign via chat

1. Open **AI Campaign Studio** and select your **contact list**.
2. Describe what you want: e.g. "Create a 3-step cold outreach campaign for SaaS founders."
3. The AI will generate templates and sequence. You can then say e.g. "Set daily limit to 30" or "Use timezone America/New_York" before launching.
4. When ready, **Launch** the campaign.

## Editing an existing campaign via chat

1. In AI Campaign Studio, if you have an **existing campaign** in context (e.g. you opened it or selected it), you can give instructions like:
   - "Change the daily limit to 50"
   - "Set timezone to Europe/London"
   - "Increase follow-up delay to 3 days"
   - "Rename this campaign to Q2 Outreach"
2. The AI returns only the **fields to change** (e.g. daily_limit, timezone, follow_up_delay_days, name). Pigeon applies these updates to the campaign.
3. Changes take effect for future sends; already-queued emails may still use the previous settings.

## What can be updated

- **Name** — Campaign name.
- **daily_limit** — Daily send cap.
- **follow_up_delay_days** — Delay between sequence steps.
- **timezone** — For send time window.

You cannot change contact list or contact IDs via these chat commands; use the campaign edit page for that.

## Summary

Use AI Campaign Studio chat to create campaigns from a description or to update an existing campaign's name, daily limit, timezone, and follow-up delay.

title: How to Set Up AI (LLM) Providers for AI Campaign Studio
content:
## Why configure an LLM?

**AI Campaign Studio** generates email templates and campaign content using an **AI/LLM provider** (e.g. OpenAI). For the Studio to work, at least one provider must be configured in Pigeon. You do this in **Settings → Integrations** (or the AI/LLM section).

## Where to configure

1. Go to **Settings** (sidebar) and open the **Integrations** tab.
2. Find the **AI** or **LLM** or **AI Campaign Studio** section (name may vary).
3. You will see options to add or edit **LLM configs**: provider (e.g. OpenAI), API key, and optionally model name.

## Step 1: Get an API key

- For **OpenAI**: sign up at [OpenAI](https://platform.openai.com/), go to API keys, and create a key. Copy it; you will paste it into Pigeon.
- For other providers (if supported): follow that provider's docs to get an API key or endpoint.

## Step 2: Add the config in Pigeon

1. In Settings → Integrations → AI/LLM, click **Add** or **Add LLM config**.
2. Select **Provider** (e.g. OpenAI).
3. Enter your **API key** (paste; the app stores it securely and does not show it again).
4. If there is a **Model** field, choose the model you want (e.g. gpt-4o-mini).
5. Save. The config appears in the list and can be used by AI Campaign Studio.

## Step 3: Use in AI Campaign Studio

1. Open **AI Campaign Studio** and generate a template or campaign.
2. If multiple configs exist, you may be able to **choose which LLM** to use for that request.
3. If you see "No LLM configured" or generation fails, go back to Settings → Integrations and add or check your API key.

## Troubleshooting

- **Generation fails** — Ensure the API key is valid and has credits. Check Settings → Integrations → LLM configs.
- **Rate limits** — If the provider rate-limits, wait and try again or use a different model.

## Summary

Settings → Integrations → AI/LLM: add an LLM config (provider + API key, optional model). AI Campaign Studio then uses it to generate templates and campaigns.

title: Understanding Your Plan Limits: Inboxes, Campaigns, and Gmail Accounts
content:
## What are plan limits?

Your Pigeon **plan** defines the maximum number of **inboxes**, **campaigns**, and **Gmail (Google) accounts** you can use. Staying within these limits keeps your account in good standing and avoids upgrade prompts when you hit a cap.

## Where to see limits and usage

- **Dashboard** — Often shows usage vs limit (e.g. inboxes used, campaigns, domains).
- **Settings → Billing** — Shows your current plan and limits (e.g. max Google accounts, max inboxes, max campaigns).
- **Campaigns** — If you are at the campaign limit, the **New campaign** button may show an upgrade prompt or Premium badge.
- **Settings → Integrations → Gmail** — Shows how many Gmail accounts you have vs the plan limit (e.g. "2 / 5 Google accounts").

## Common limits

- **max_google_accounts** — How many Gmail accounts you can connect. If 0, your plan does not include Gmail; use SMTP only.
- **Inboxes** — Total sending inboxes (Gmail + SMTP). Some plans cap this number.
- **Campaigns** — Maximum number of campaigns (active + paused + draft).
- **Warmup** — Whether warmup is included; some plans include it, others don't.

## What happens at the limit

- **Gmail** — You cannot add another Gmail account until you upgrade or remove one.
- **Inboxes** — Same: add more only after upgrade or removing an inbox.
- **Campaigns** — You must upgrade or pause/delete a campaign to create a new one.

## Tips

- Check **Get Started** and **Pricing** for your plan's limits.
- Use **Dashboard** and **Settings → Billing** to track usage so you can plan upgrades or clean up unused resources.

## Summary

Plan limits cap Gmail accounts, inboxes, and campaigns. View them on the Dashboard and in Settings → Billing; upgrade or remove resources when you hit a limit.
excerpt: Your plan caps Gmail accounts, inboxes, and campaigns. See usage on the Dashboard and in Settings → Billing.

title: How Per-Inbox Daily Limits Work (Reset Time, New Inboxes)
content:
## What are per-inbox daily limits?

Each **sending inbox** in Pigeon can have a **daily send limit** (e.g. 50 emails per day). This protects deliverability by capping how much one inbox sends in 24 hours. Pigeon also applies a **safer pattern** for new or at-cap inboxes.

## Reset time

- Per-inbox limits **reset at midnight UTC** every day.
- After reset, the "sent today" count for that inbox goes back to 0 and the inbox can send again up to its daily limit.
- Your **campaign** daily limit and **send time window** (e.g. 9–17 in your timezone) still apply; we only send during that window and never exceed the campaign or per-inbox cap.

## New inboxes (<7 days)

- For inboxes **newer than 7 days**, Pigeon uses a **safer sending pattern**: we avoid maxing out the daily limit and may use longer gaps between sends. This helps build reputation.
- Once the inbox is older and warmed (e.g. status **Ready**), you can rely on the full daily limit within your campaign settings.

## Near daily cap

- When an inbox is **near its daily cap** (e.g. 48/50 sent today), we may slow or stop using it for the rest of the day and use other inboxes in the rotation. After midnight UTC, that inbox is available again.

## Where you see this

- **Inbox Accounts** — Each inbox shows **Sent today** (or similar). Use this to see how much of the daily limit is used.
- **Campaigns** — The campaign's **daily limit** is the total across all selected inboxes; we distribute sends and respect each inbox's per-inbox limit and reset.
- **Sent tooltip** — On campaign or inbox views, the (?) or info icon explains rotation, human-like timing, and daily limits.

## Summary

Per-inbox daily limits reset at **midnight UTC**. New inboxes (<7 days) get a safer pattern; near-cap inboxes may be used less until reset. Check Inbox Accounts for "Sent today."
excerpt: Per-inbox daily limits reset at midnight UTC; new inboxes get a safer pattern. Check Inbox Accounts for Sent today.

title: Campaign Daily Limit vs Per-Inbox Limits: How They Work Together
content:
## Two types of daily limits

When you run a campaign, two limits apply: the **campaign daily limit** (total emails per day for that campaign) and the **per-inbox daily limit** (max each inbox can send per day). Pigeon enforces **both** so you never exceed either.

## Campaign daily limit

- Set when you **create or edit** a campaign (e.g. 100 emails per day).
- This is the **total** number of emails that campaign can send in one day across **all** selected inboxes.
- We spread sends across the send time window (e.g. 9–17) and rotate across inboxes (round-robin or random).

## Per-inbox daily limit

- Each **inbox** has its own daily cap (e.g. 50 per day), set in Inbox Accounts or when adding the inbox.
- No single inbox will send more than its per-inbox limit in one day (reset at midnight UTC).
- If you have 2 inboxes with 50 each and a campaign limit of 100, we can send up to 100 that day (50 + 50). If one inbox already sent 50, we use only the other until the next day.

## How they work together

- We **never** send more than the **campaign** daily limit in one day.
- We **never** send more than each inbox's **per-inbox** limit in one day.
- So effective daily send = min(campaign limit, sum of available per-inbox capacity). Example: campaign 200, two inboxes 50 each → we send at most 100 that day (50 + 50).

## Tips

- Set **campaign** limit to match your goals; set **per-inbox** limits to protect each inbox's reputation.
- Use enough inboxes so that the sum of their per-inbox limits is at least your campaign limit if you want to hit the campaign cap every day.

## Summary

Campaign daily limit = total per day for that campaign. Per-inbox limit = max per inbox per day. We enforce both; effective send is the minimum of campaign limit and available inbox capacity.
excerpt: Campaign daily limit is total per day; per-inbox limit caps each inbox. Pigeon enforces both.

title: How to View Campaign Stats and Start or Pause a Campaign
content:
## Where to see campaign stats

1. Go to **Campaigns** in the sidebar and click a **campaign** in the list (or open it from the Dashboard).
2. You land on the **campaign detail** page. There you see:
   - **Sent** — How many emails have been sent for this campaign.
   - **Opened** — How many were opened (if tracking is enabled).
   - **Replied** — How many recipients replied.
   - **Open rate** / **Reply rate** — Percentages.
   - **Status** — e.g. Running, Paused, Completed, Draft.
   - **Health score** — If your plan shows it, a score for this campaign's sending health.

## Start a campaign

1. On the campaign detail page, if the campaign is **Draft** or **Paused**, you will see a **Start** or **Resume** button.
2. Click **Start** (or **Resume**). Confirm if prompted.
3. The campaign begins sending according to its schedule and daily limit. Status changes to **Running**.

## Pause a campaign

1. On the campaign detail page, if the campaign is **Running**, click **Pause**.
2. Confirm. The campaign stops sending; recipients who already got some emails will not get the next steps until you resume.
3. Status changes to **Paused**. You can **Resume** later from the same page.

## Other actions

- **Edit** — Change name, contact list, inboxes, sequence, daily limit, or send window. Some changes apply only to future sends.
- **Contacts** — View or change the campaign's audience (contact list).
- **Actions** — Depending on your plan, other actions may appear (e.g. duplicate, archive).

## Summary

Campaigns → select campaign → view Sent, Opened, Replied, rates, status. Use **Start**/ **Resume** to run, **Pause** to stop.

title: How to View or Change a Campaign's Audience (Contact List)
content:
## Where to see the campaign's audience

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open a campaign (click its name or row).
2. On the campaign detail page, look for **Contacts**, **Audience**, or **Contact list** — or open the **Contacts** tab/subpage for that campaign (e.g. **Campaigns → [Campaign name] → Contacts**).
3. You will see which **contact list** is used and how many contacts are in it. You may also see a list of contacts or a preview.

## Change the contact list

- If the campaign is still **Draft** or has not started, you can often **change the contact list** from the campaign edit page (Campaigns → Edit). Select a different list and save. Only contacts in the new list will receive the campaign.
- If the campaign has **already started**, changing the list may affect only **future** sends (recipients who haven't received any email yet). Already-sent or in-progress recipients are usually not removed. Check the in-app wording when you change the list.

## Add or remove contacts

- To **add** contacts to the audience, add them to the **contact list** that the campaign uses (Contacts → open that list → Import or add contacts). The campaign will then include them in future sends (subject to schedule and limits).
- To **exclude** someone, remove them from that contact list or add them to **Manual Block / Unblock** (Contacts → Manual Block / Unblock) so they never receive campaigns.

## Summary

Campaign detail → Contacts/Audience: see the contact list and size. Change list on the campaign edit page (draft or for future sends); add/remove contacts via the contact list or block list.

title: What Is ReplyFlow and How to Set It Up for Campaigns
content:
## What is ReplyFlow?

**ReplyFlow** in Pigeon refers to how **replies** to your campaign emails are handled: where they are delivered (reply-to address) and how you can read and manage them inside Pigeon (e.g. in the **Inbox** tab). Setting it up ensures replies go to the right place and appear in your Inbox.

## Where to set ReplyFlow

When you **create or edit a campaign** (Campaigns → New or Edit), one of the steps is **ReplyFlow** (or Reply-To / Reply to address). There you choose:
- **Use default** — Use the reply-to address set in **Settings → Integrations** (default reply-to).
- **Specific Gmail** — Replies go to a chosen Gmail account (one of your connected Gmail inboxes).
- **Specific IMAP** — Replies go to an IMAP mailbox you configured in Settings → Integrations → Reply-To IMAP.

## Default reply-to (Settings)

1. Go to **Settings** → **Integrations**.
2. Find **Reply-To** or **Campaign replies** / **Default reply-to**.
3. Set the default: e.g. a Gmail account or an IMAP config. Save. New campaigns will use this unless you override per campaign.

## Per-campaign override

1. In the campaign wizard, go to the **ReplyFlow** step.
2. Select **Specific Gmail** or **Specific IMAP** and pick the mailbox you want for this campaign.
3. Save the campaign. Replies to that campaign will go to that address and, if it's a connected Gmail or configured IMAP, they will appear in **Inbox**.

## Why it matters

- So you **receive** replies in one place (Gmail or IMAP) and see them in Pigeon Inbox.
- So **Pigeon can match** replies to the correct campaign (via headers).

## Summary

ReplyFlow = where campaign replies go. Set default in Settings → Integrations; override per campaign in the ReplyFlow step (Gmail or IMAP).
excerpt: ReplyFlow is where campaign replies go. Set default in Settings → Integrations; override per campaign in the ReplyFlow step.

title: How to Manage Warmup Send Templates
content:
## What are warmup send templates?

**Warmup** in Pigeon sends a controlled volume of emails from your inboxes to build reputation. The **content** of those warmup emails can be defined by **warmup send templates**: subject and body that the system uses when sending warmup messages. You manage these under **Warmup → Manage templates** (or Warmup templates).

## Where to find them

1. Click **Warmup** in the sidebar.
2. Open **Manage templates** (or **Warmup templates**).
3. You will see a list of warmup send templates. Each has a name, subject, and body (and possibly a status).

## Create a warmup template

1. On the Warmup templates page, click **New** or **Create template**.
2. Enter a **name** (e.g. "Default warmup") and the **subject** and **body** for the warmup emails. The content is usually neutral (e.g. "Warmup message") so recipients (often internal or partner addresses) know it's warmup.
3. Save. The new template is available for warmup; you may need to assign it to an inbox or it becomes the default depending on your plan.

## Edit or delete

- **Edit** — Open a template and change name, subject, or body. Save. Warmup will use the updated content for new sends.
- **Delete** — Remove a template you no longer need. Ensure no inbox is currently using it, or assign another template first.

## Use with warmup

- When you **start warmup** for an inbox (Warmup page), you may be able to choose which warmup template to use. Select the one you created or the default.
- Warmup sends are automatic; you don't run campaigns from the warmup template — it's only for the warmup process.

## Summary

Warmup → Manage templates: create, edit, or delete warmup send templates (subject + body). Use them when starting warmup for an inbox.
excerpt: Create, edit, and delete warmup send templates under Warmup → Manage templates; use them when starting warmup for an inbox.

title: How to Use Template Prompts for AI-Generated Emails
content:
## What are Template Prompts?

**Template Prompts** (under **Templates** in the sidebar) are pre-written **prompt ideas** you can copy and use in **AI Campaign Studio** to generate email templates. They give you a starting point so you don't have to write the prompt from scratch (e.g. "Cold outreach to SaaS founders" or "Follow-up after no reply").

## Where to find them

1. Click **Templates** in the sidebar.
2. Open **Template Prompts** (or **Prompts**).
3. You will see a list of prompts: each has a name, description, and the full **markdown/text** of the prompt.

## How to use a prompt

1. **Copy** the prompt text (use the Copy button or select and copy).
2. Go to **AI Campaign Studio**.
3. **Paste** the prompt into the description/prompt field (or adapt it with your audience and details).
4. Select your **contact list** and click **Generate**. The AI will produce a template (subject + body) based on that prompt and your list's merge variables.
5. Edit the result if needed, run compliance check, then save as a template or use in a campaign.

## Tips

- Combine a Template Prompt with **links** or **additional details** in AI Campaign Studio for more tailored copy.
- Use **Templates → Template Guide** for merge variables and compliance (unsubscribe, spam words) so the generated template is compliant.

## Summary

Templates → Template Prompts: copy a prompt, paste it in AI Campaign Studio, select list, generate, then edit and use the template in a campaign.
excerpt: Copy prompts from Templates → Template Prompts, paste in AI Campaign Studio, and generate compliant templates for your list.

title: Understanding the Activity Feed: Sends, Opens, Clicks, and Replies
content:
## What is the Activity feed?

The **Activity** page in Pigeon shows **recent activity** across your campaigns and inboxes: sends, opens, link clicks, and replies. It gives you a single timeline of what's happening so you can see engagement and troubleshoot.

## Where to find it

1. Click **Activity** in the sidebar (if your plan includes it).
2. You will see a list of events, newest first. Each event usually shows: **type** (send, open, click, reply), **contact** or **email**, **campaign** or **inbox**, and **time** (e.g. "2 minutes ago").

## Event types

- **Send** — An email was sent from one of your campaigns (to a contact).
- **Open** — A recipient opened the email (if open tracking is enabled).
- **Click** — A recipient clicked a link in the email (if click tracking is enabled).
- **Reply** — A recipient replied to a campaign email; the reply may appear in **Inbox** as well.

## How to use it

- **Monitor engagement** — See opens and clicks to judge subject lines and content.
- **Spot replies** — Quick view of who replied; then go to **Inbox** for the full thread.
- **Debug** — Confirm that sends are happening and that opens/clicks are recorded (if tracking is on).

## Limits

- The feed may show only the last N events (e.g. 50). For full analytics, use **Analytics** and **Sending Behavior** (Tracking).

## Summary

Activity (sidebar) shows a timeline of sends, opens, clicks, and replies. Use it to monitor engagement and spot replies; use Analytics for deeper stats.
excerpt: The Activity page shows a timeline of sends, opens, clicks, and replies across campaigns; use it to monitor engagement.

title: How to Contact Support and Create a Support Ticket
content:
## How to get help

Pigeon offers **Support** (tickets) so you can ask questions, report issues, or request features. You create and manage tickets from **Support** in the sidebar (or **Tickets**).

## Where to find Support

1. Click **Support** (or **Tickets**) in the sidebar.
2. You will see your **ticket list**: open, in progress, resolved, closed. You can open an existing ticket or create a new one.

## Create a new ticket

1. On the Support/Tickets page, click **New ticket** or **Create ticket**.
2. Enter a **subject** (short title) and **message** (describe your issue or question in detail).
3. If there are fields for **priority** (e.g. Low, Medium, High, Urgent) or **category**, fill them in.
4. Submit. The ticket is created and appears in your list with status **Open**. Support will respond via the ticket (you may get an email notification).

## What to include in your message

- **What you did** — e.g. "I tried to connect Gmail via OAuth."
- **What happened** — e.g. "I see 'Redirect URI mismatch'."
- **What you expected** — e.g. "I expected to be redirected back to Pigeon."
- **Screenshots or IDs** — If helpful, attach a screenshot or mention campaign/domain/inbox ID (no passwords or API keys).

## Manage tickets

- **Open** a ticket to read replies and add follow-up messages.
- **Status** may change to In progress, Resolved, or Closed. You can reopen or add a comment if the issue persists.

## Summary

Support (sidebar) → Create ticket: add subject and message (and priority/category). Include what you did, what happened, and what you expected. Track replies in the ticket list.

title: How to Add a New Inbox: Daily Limit, Bulk Add, and Auto Warmup
content:
## Where to add a new inbox

1. Go to **Inbox Accounts** in the sidebar and click **Add Inbox** or **New**, or open **Inbox Accounts → New** (or **inboxes/new**) if you have a dedicated page.
2. You will choose **Gmail** or **SMTP** and then fill in the details.

## Gmail

- **Connect with Google** (OAuth) or **Connect via App Password** — Same as in Settings → Integrations → Gmail. After connecting, the account appears in Inbox Accounts. You can set a **daily limit** for that inbox (e.g. 50) in inbox settings if the page allows.

## SMTP (domain inbox)

1. Select **SMTP** and choose your **verified domain**.
2. Enter **email address** (e.g. sales@yourcompany.com), **SMTP host**, **port**, **username**, **password** (or API key).
3. **Daily limit** — Set how many emails this inbox can send per day (e.g. 50). We use this and reset at midnight UTC.
4. **Bulk add** — If the page has a **Bulk** mode, you can add multiple SMTP inboxes at once (e.g. paste a list of usernames or emails). Each gets the same SMTP host/port/credentials and daily limit unless you override.
5. **Auto warmup** — If your plan includes warmup, you can enable **Auto warmup** so this inbox starts warming as soon as it's added. Otherwise, start warmup manually from the **Warmup** page.
6. Save. New inboxes appear in **Inbox Accounts** and may show status **Warm up required** or **Warming**.

## After adding

- Check **Inbox Accounts** for status and **Sent today**.
- Use **Warmup** to start or monitor warmup. When status is **Ready**, use the inbox in campaigns.

## Summary

Inbox Accounts → Add Inbox: Gmail (OAuth or App Password) or SMTP. For SMTP, set daily limit, use Bulk add if needed, and enable Auto warmup when available.
excerpt: Add a new inbox from Inbox Accounts: Gmail or SMTP; for SMTP set daily limit, use Bulk add, and enable Auto warmup if available.

title: How to Bulk Add SMTP Inbox Accounts
content:
## When to use bulk add

If you have many **SMTP inboxes** on the same domain and same provider (same host, port, credentials pattern), you can **bulk add** them in one go instead of adding each inbox one by one. This saves time when onboarding many addresses (e.g. sales1@, sales2@, ...).

## Where to find bulk add

1. Go to **Inbox Accounts** and click **Add Inbox** or **New** (or open **inboxes/new**).
2. Select **SMTP** and your **verified domain**.
3. Look for **Bulk** or **Bulk add** mode (e.g. a toggle or tab: Single vs Bulk). Switch to **Bulk**.

## How to bulk add

1. Enter the **SMTP host**, **port**, **username**, and **password** (or API key) that apply to all inboxes. Some providers use the same password for all; others use per-address credentials — follow your provider's docs.
2. In the bulk section, enter the **list of email addresses or usernames** (e.g. one per line: sales1@yourcompany.com, sales2@yourcompany.com, or just sales1, sales2 if the domain is already set).
3. Set a **daily limit** per inbox (e.g. 50) if the form allows (it may apply to all in the batch).
4. If available, enable **Auto warmup** for the new inboxes.
5. Click **Add** or **Create**. Pigeon will create one inbox per line/entry. They appear in **Inbox Accounts**; check for any that failed (e.g. invalid address or credentials).

## After bulk add

- Go to **Inbox Accounts** and **Warmup** to start warmup for the new inboxes (or they may auto-start if you enabled Auto warmup).
- Set or adjust **daily limits** per inbox in inbox settings if needed.

## Summary

Inbox Accounts → Add Inbox → SMTP → Bulk: enter shared SMTP details and a list of addresses/usernames; add all at once, then start warmup.
excerpt: Use Bulk add when adding many SMTP inboxes: enter shared host/credentials and a list of addresses to create them in one go.

title: Domain Verification Failed: Common Fixes (SPF, DKIM, MX)
content:
## Why verification fails

**Domain verification** in Pigeon checks that the right **DNS records** (SPF, DKIM, MX) are present for your domain. If verification fails, it's usually because a record is missing, wrong, or not yet propagated. Fix the records and try **Verify** again.

## Check the exact values

1. In **Domains**, select your domain and open the **DNS records** or **Verification** section.
2. Pigeon shows the **exact** Type, Name/Host, and **Value** you must add. Copy them exactly — no extra spaces, no typos.
3. At your **DNS provider** (e.g. Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap), open DNS management for this domain and compare each record.

## SPF (TXT)

- **Only one SPF (TXT) record** per domain (or subdomain) is allowed. If you already have an SPF record, you must **merge** Pigeon's include (e.g. `include:sendgrid.net` or similar) into your existing SPF value. Do not create two separate SPF TXT records.
- Format is usually: `v=spf1 include:... ~all` or `-all`. Add Pigeon's include inside the same string.

## DKIM (TXT)

- DKIM is usually one or more **TXT** records with a specific **name** (e.g. `pigeon._domainkey` or what Pigeon shows) and a long **value**. Copy name and value exactly. Some providers want the value in one line; others allow multiple lines — follow the provider's UI.

## MX (if required)

- If Pigeon asks for **MX** records (e.g. for receiving), add the **priority** and **value** (e.g. `mx.sendgrid.net`) as shown. Do not remove existing MX records if you need them for receiving email elsewhere; you may need to add Pigeon's MX with a lower priority or adjust according to your setup.

## Propagation

- DNS changes can take **minutes to 48 hours** to propagate. If you just added records, wait 15–30 minutes and click **Verify** again. If it still fails, double-check values and try again later.

## Summary

Copy DNS values exactly from Domains; fix SPF (merge if needed), DKIM (exact name/value), and MX. Wait for propagation and verify again.
excerpt: Fix verification by copying DNS values exactly, merging SPF if needed, and waiting for propagation before verifying again.

title: Understanding Campaign and Inbox Health Scores
content:
## What is a health score?

Pigeon may show a **health score** (e.g. 0–100) for **campaigns** and **inboxes**. This score reflects how well the campaign or inbox is doing from a **deliverability and reputation** perspective: sending pattern, bounce/complaint signals, warmup state, and similar factors. A higher score is better.

## Where you see it

- **Campaigns** list or **campaign detail** — A campaign may have a health score badge or tooltip.
- **Inbox Accounts** or **Warmup** — An inbox may show a health or reputation indicator.
- **Health score tooltip** — Hover or click the (?) or info icon next to the score to see a short explanation of what affects it.

## What affects the score

- **Sending volume** — Sending too much too fast (especially from new or cold inboxes) can lower the score.
- **Warmup** — Inboxes that are **Ready** or well warmed tend to have better scores; **Warm up required** or **Warning** can reduce it.
- **Bounces and complaints** — High bounce or spam complaint rates can lower the score.
- **Consistency** — Steady, human-like sending (daily limits, send windows, rotation) tends to support a good score.

## What to do

- **Green / high** — Keep doing what you're doing; stay within daily limits and send windows.
- **Amber / medium** — Review Sending Behavior and warmup; consider lowering daily limit or pausing campaigns until warmup improves.
- **Red / low** — Reduce sending from that campaign or inbox, ensure warmup is running or complete, and fix any bounce/complaint issues (e.g. list hygiene, block list).

## Summary

Health score reflects deliverability and reputation. Check it on campaigns and inboxes; use the tooltip for details. Improve by warming inboxes, respecting limits, and keeping bounces and complaints low.
excerpt: Health score reflects deliverability and reputation for campaigns and inboxes. Use the tooltip for details and improve with warmup and limits.

title: How to Add Multiple Steps and Follow-up Delays to a Campaign
content:
## What are sequence steps?

A **campaign** in Pigeon is an **email sequence**: one or more **steps** (emails) sent to each contact. The **first** step is usually sent when the contact enters the campaign (or when the campaign runs); **follow-up** steps are sent after a **delay** (e.g. 2 days, 5 days). You add steps and set delays when creating or editing the campaign.

## Where to add steps

1. Go to **Campaigns** → **New campaign** or **Edit** an existing one.
2. Open the **Email Sequence** (or **Sequence**) step/tab.
3. You will see a list of steps (e.g. Step 1, Step 2). Each step has a **template** (subject + body) and a **delay** (e.g. 0 days, 2 days, 5 days).

## Add a step

1. Click **Add step** or **Add email** (or the + icon).
2. Select a **template** for this step. You can use an existing template or create one (Templates).
3. Set the **delay**: 0 for the first email (sends immediately when the contact is due), or e.g. 2 for "send 2 days after the previous step." Delays are usually in **days**; the system schedules the next step relative to when the previous one was sent.
4. Save. Repeat to add more follow-ups (e.g. Step 1: 0 days, Step 2: 2 days, Step 3: 5 days).

## Reorder or remove

- **Reorder** — Drag steps or use up/down to change the order. The first step (delay 0) is the initial email; the rest are follow-ups.
- **Remove** — Delete a step you don't need. Contacts who already received that step are unaffected; those who haven't will skip it.

## Best practices

- Keep the **first** step delay at **0** so the first email goes out as soon as the campaign runs for that contact.
- Use **2–5 days** between follow-ups so you don't look spammy. Adjust by audience and goal.
- Use **merge variables** and **unsubscribe** in every template. Run **compliance check** before launching.

## Summary

Campaigns → Sequence: add steps (template + delay). First step delay 0; follow-ups 2–5 days typical. Reorder or remove steps as needed.
excerpt: In the campaign sequence, add steps with a template and delay (0 for first, 2–5 days for follow-ups); reorder or remove as needed.

title: How to Use Spintax in Email Templates
content:
## What is Spintax?

**Spintax** (spin syntax) lets you define **multiple options** for a word or phrase; when the email is sent, **one option is picked at random** per recipient. That way each contact gets a slightly different line (e.g. "Hi" vs "Hello" vs "Hey") so your copy feels more natural and less template-like. Pigeon supports Spintax in both **subject** and **body** of templates.

## Syntax

Use **pipe-separated options** inside **curly braces**: `{Option A|Option B|Option C}`. For each send, one of the options is chosen. Example:

- `{Hi|Hello|Hey} {{first_name}},` → One recipient gets "Hi John,", another "Hello Jane,", another "Hey Alex,".
- Subject: `{Quick question|One thing}| about {{company}}` → Random first part, then the merge variable.

## Where to use it

- **Subject line** — Vary the opening or call-to-action: `{Re: Intro|Following up}| {{first_name}}`.
- **Body** — Greetings, transitions, or CTAs: `{Hope you're well|Just reaching out|I wanted to connect}.`
- **With merge variables** — You can mix: `{{first_name}}, {thanks|thank you} for your time.`

## Best practices

- **Don't over-spin** — A few spins per email add variety; too many can look odd or trigger filters.
- **Keep options similar in length and tone** — So readability and compliance (spam words, link count) stay consistent.
- **Test** — Send a few test emails or preview with sample data to see how spins look.

## Compliance

Spintax is evaluated **after** merge variables. Make sure **no option** contains spam words or exceeds link/image limits (Settings → Compliance). The Template Guide and compliance check apply to the final content.

## Summary

Use `{Option A|Option B|Option C}` in subject and body for random variation per send. Use sparingly and keep options compliant.
excerpt: Use {Option A|Option B} Spintax in subject and body for random variation per email; keep options compliant and don't over-spin.

title: How to Duplicate a Campaign
content:
## Why duplicate a campaign?

**Duplicating** a campaign creates a **copy** with the same settings (contact list, sequence, inboxes, daily limit, send window, reply-to). You can then change the name, tweak the sequence or audience, and launch it as a new campaign without re-entering everything. Useful for running similar outreach to a different list or A/B testing a variant.

## Where to duplicate

1. Go to **Campaigns** in the sidebar.
2. Find the campaign you want to copy in the list.
3. Use the **Duplicate** action (e.g. from the row menu, three dots, or a Duplicate button). Click it.

## What gets copied

- **Campaign name** — Usually copied with a suffix like "(Copy)" or you can rename when editing.
- **Contact list** — The same list is selected (you can change it when editing the duplicate).
- **Email sequence** — All steps (templates + delays) are copied.
- **Sender** — Gmail or SMTP and the same inbox selection.
- **Schedule** — Timezone, send time window, daily limit.
- **ReplyFlow** — Reply-to setting.

## What to do after duplicating

1. The new campaign appears in the list, usually in **Draft** status.
2. Open it and **Edit** to change the name, switch the contact list, or adjust the sequence before launching.
3. When ready, **Start** or **Launch** the campaign.

## Notes

- Duplication does **not** copy **tracking data** (opens, clicks, replies) or **send history** — only the configuration.
- You are subject to **plan limits** (max campaigns); if you're at the limit, you must upgrade or pause/delete another campaign before duplicating.

## Summary

Campaigns → select campaign → Duplicate. Edit the new draft (name, list, sequence) and launch when ready.
excerpt: Duplicate a campaign from the Campaigns list to copy settings; edit the new draft (name, list, sequence) and launch.

title: Understanding Campaign Jobs and How to Stop a Send
content:
## What are campaign jobs?

When a campaign **runs**, Pigeon processes sends in **jobs** (batches). Each job has a status: **Pending**, **Running**, **Completed**, **Failed**, or **Cancelled**. You can see active and recent jobs on the **Campaign Actions** (or **Jobs**) page for that campaign and, if needed, **stop** a running job so no more emails go out from that batch.

## Where to see jobs

1. Go to **Campaigns** and open a campaign (click its name).
2. Open **Actions** or **Jobs** (e.g. Campaigns → [Campaign name] → Actions).
3. You will see a list of jobs: status, start time, progress (e.g. sent count), and actions (e.g. **Stop** for a running job).

## Stop a running job

1. Find the job with status **Running**.
2. Click **Stop** (or **Cancel** / **Stop job**). Confirm if prompted.
3. The job stops; no further emails are sent for that batch. Contacts who already received an email from that job are unaffected; those still in the queue for that job will not receive it unless a new job is started.

## When to stop a job

- You launched the campaign by mistake and want to halt immediately.
- You noticed a wrong template, list, or inbox and want to fix the campaign before more sends.
- You hit a limit or got an alert and want to pause sending.

## After stopping

- The campaign may still show as **Running** if other jobs are pending. **Pause** the campaign from the campaign detail page to stop all future sends.
- Edit the campaign (sequence, list, inboxes) as needed, then **Resume** when you're ready, or leave it paused.

## Summary

Campaign → Actions: view jobs and **Stop** a running job to halt that batch. Use **Pause** on the campaign to stop all sends.
excerpt: View campaign jobs under Campaign → Actions; use Stop to halt a running job. Pause the campaign to stop all sends.

title: How to Edit an Existing Email Template
content:
## Where to edit a template

1. Go to **Templates** in the sidebar (Template Management).
2. Find the template you want to change in the list and click it (or click **Edit** / the pencil icon).
3. You will open the **template editor** with the current name, subject, and body.

## What you can change

- **Name** — So you can find the template easily (e.g. "Cold outreach – intro v2").
- **Subject line** — Update the subject; you can add or change merge variables (e.g. {{first_name}}, {{company}}) and Spintax.
- **Body** — Update the email body (plain text or HTML). Keep or add merge variables and the **unsubscribe** placeholder (see Template Guide for the exact placeholder).

## After saving

- **Campaigns already using this template** will send the **updated** subject and body for **future** sends (e.g. follow-up steps that haven't been sent yet). Already-sent emails are unchanged.
- If you run **compliance check** (spam words, links, images), fix any issues before saving so existing and new campaigns stay compliant.

## Best practices

- Don't remove the **unsubscribe** line; it's required for compliance.
- Use **Templates → Template Guide** for merge variables and compliance limits.
- If you want to keep the old version, **duplicate** the template first (if the option exists), then edit the copy.

## Summary

Templates → select template → Edit. Change name, subject, body; save. Campaigns using this template will use the new content for future sends.
excerpt: Templates → select template → Edit to change name, subject, and body. Campaigns using it get the new content for future sends.

title: Warmup credits are reply-based
content:
## Warmup settlement rule

Warmup credit settlement is **reply-based**.

- A warmup rental places credits in **held** status.
- Credits release to the provider when a **reply** is detected.
- If no reply is detected within about **48 hours**, the renter is refunded and the held amount expires.

## What changed

Warmup no longer relies on click/open tracking pixels or wrapped tracking links for credit qualification.

## Where to check status

- **Warmup logs** for sent/replied visibility.
- **Warmup network** for shared pool balance/held credits.
- **Rent credits/activity** for held, released, and refunded entries.
excerpt: Warmup credits now release on reply only; no open/click tracking requirement for warmup settlement.

title: Understanding Pigeon Plans and Pricing
content:
## Where to see plans and pricing

- **Pricing page** — From the marketing site or **Pricing** in the footer/menu you can see available plans (e.g. Free, Pro, Premium), features, and price.
- **Settings → Billing** — Inside the app you see your **current plan**, **usage** (e.g. inboxes used, campaigns, Gmail accounts), and **limits**. You can upgrade or manage subscription here (or via the link provided).

## What plans typically include

- **Inboxes** — Max number of sending inboxes (Gmail + SMTP).
- **Gmail (Google accounts)** — Max Gmail accounts you can connect; some plans allow 0 (SMTP only).
- **Campaigns** — Max number of campaigns (active + paused + draft).
- **Domains** — Max verified domains (varies by plan).
- **Warmup** — Whether inbox warmup is included and how many inboxes can be warmed.
- **Templates, contacts, analytics** — Usually included; limits may apply (e.g. contact list size).

## Upgrade and downgrade

- **Upgrade** — From Settings → Billing (or Pricing), choose a higher plan. You may be charged a prorated amount or at the next billing cycle depending on your provider.
- **Downgrade** — If you switch to a lower plan, you may need to stay within the new limits (e.g. remove extra inboxes or campaigns). The app or billing page will explain when the change takes effect.

## Trial and refunds

- **Free trial** — Some plans offer a trial; check **Get Started** or **Pricing** for eligibility. When the trial ends, you may be moved to Free or asked to subscribe.
- **Refunds** — See the **Refund** or **Terms** page (footer) for the refund policy.

## Summary

View plans on the Pricing page; view your plan and usage in Settings → Billing. Upgrade or downgrade from Billing; stay within limits when downgrading.
excerpt: See plans on the Pricing page and your usage in Settings → Billing. Upgrade or downgrade from Billing; respect limits when downgrading.

title: Contact Import: File Size, Format, and Duplicate Handling
content:
## File format and size

- **Supported formats**: **.csv**, **.xlsx**, **.xls**. One row per contact; first row is usually headers (column names).
- **Max file size**: Typically **10 MB**. If your file is larger, split it into multiple files or reduce columns/rows and import in batches.
- **Encoding**: Use UTF-8 when possible so special characters (accents, symbols) import correctly.

## Required and optional columns

- **Email** is **required**. Every row must have a valid email address; invalid or empty emails may be skipped or cause the row to fail.
- **Optional**: First name, last name, company, industry, location, and custom fields. Map them in the import step (Contacts → Import → map columns to Pigeon fields).

## Duplicate handling

- **Same email in the file** — If you have duplicate emails in the same file, the importer may keep one and skip the rest, or update the same contact (depending on the app behaviour). Check the import summary after upload to see "Imported" vs "Skipped" or "Updated."
- **Email already in the list** — When you add contacts to an **existing list**, contacts whose email is already in that list may be **skipped** (not duplicated) or **updated** (if you have update-on-import). The import result will show how many were added vs skipped.
- **Across lists** — The same email can exist in **different** contact lists; each list is independent. A contact is not automatically removed from another list when you import into a new list.

## Tips

- **Download the example CSV** from the import page to see the recommended format and headers.
- **Remove invalid emails** before importing to avoid high skip counts.
- **Back up** important lists before large imports or overwrites.

## Summary

Use CSV or Excel, max 10 MB; email required. Duplicates in-file or already-in-list may be skipped or updated; check the import summary.
excerpt: Import supports CSV/Excel up to 10 MB; email required. Duplicates may be skipped or updated—check the import summary.

title: How to Reset Your Password
content:
## When to reset your password

If you **forgot your password** or want to **change it** for security, use the **Forgot password** flow. Pigeon will send you an email with a link to set a new password.

## Step 1: Request a reset link

1. On the **Login** page, click **Forgot password?** (or the equivalent link).
2. Enter the **email address** associated with your Pigeon account.
3. Click **Send** or **Reset password**. If that email is in our system, you will receive a message with a **reset link** (valid for a limited time, e.g. 1 hour).

## Step 2: Set a new password

1. Open the email and click the **reset link**. You will be taken to a **Reset password** page (or Set new password).
2. Enter your **new password** (and confirm it if the form has two fields). Use a strong password: mix of letters, numbers, and symbols; avoid common words.
3. Submit. Your password is updated; you can now **log in** with the new password.

## If you don't receive the email

- Check **spam** and **promotions** folders.
- Ensure you entered the same email you use to log in.
- Wait a few minutes; delivery can be delayed. Try again once; avoid requesting many resets in a short time (rate limits may apply).
- If it still fails, contact **Support** (Tickets) with your account email so we can help.

## After resetting

- **Log in** with your email and the **new** password.
- If you use **sessions** or "Remember me," you may need to log in again on some devices after a password change.

## Summary

Login → Forgot password → enter email → open reset link in email → set new password → log in with the new password.
excerpt: Use Forgot password on the login page, enter your email, then set a new password via the link sent to you.
